detail.abstract: The recent sub-prime debacle has brought 'innovative' structured credit products such as collateralized debt obligations under severe criticism. The complexity of some structured finance securities and difficulties in understanding their risks has been a common theme. This paper argues that CDO-squared structures can be so complex as to make risk assessment difficult. By modeling a simplified CDO-squared structure using Monte Carlo simulation, two of the risks unique to such structures are examined: default location risk and overlap risk. Failure to take account of these risks during a distressed credit environment will result in greater than anticipated losses among senior CDO-squared tranches.(JEL: G11, G15, G24)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A

detail.abstract: Fermented aquatic foods are increasingly recognised for their potential to enhance food quality, functionality, and shelf life while supporting innovation in sustainable food systems. However, evidence on consumer perceptions and acceptance remains fragmented. This systematic scoping review synthesised evidence on consumer perceptions and acceptance of fermented aquatic foods from 30 eligible studies. Most studies originated from Asia (76.7%) and focused on shrimp/crustacean products, fermented fish products, fish sauces and fermented fish condiments, and seaweed-based products. Consumer acceptance was consistently influenced by sensory quality, particularly flavour, aroma, texture, and appearance, together with processing strategies such as starter cultures, fermentation duration, salt modification, and product formulation. Controlled fermentation generally enhanced sensory quality and overall consumer acceptance across diverse aquatic products. Despite these advances, research remained heavily centred on product optimisation, with limited investigation of consumer behaviour, purchase intention, market adoption, willingness to pay, cross-cultural differences, or sustainability perceptions. These findings indicated that successful development of fermented aquatic foods depends not only on advances in fermentation technology but also on integrating consumer perspectives throughout product innovation. Embedding consumer acceptance into product development will be essential for translating fermentation innovations into fermented aquatic foods with greater potential for wider adoption within sustainable food systems.

title: Cashing in at the Border: Developmental Frontier Localities between Central Asia and Western China

detail.abstract: Interstate borders are not just 'lines in the sand' over fixed territory but rather dynamic and subject to not only state capacity and intentionality but also local adaptations (and sometimes resistance) of central directives on borderland management. Borderland local governments in pursuit of development can contribute to significantly divergent outcomes, even on the same side of a national border. Land resources are the core element of state endurance and territorial sovereignty as well as local development; therefore land use changes are an essential indicator that can reveal the degree of discontinuity in local development in border regions. Scholarship on local governments is often constrained by a lack of data at lower-level subnational administrative units. We incorporate GIS mapping of administrative unit boundaries with highly granular remote sensing land cover data and nighttime brightness to account for local development, such as urbanization, the building of infrastructure and human capital accumulation, to measure how discontinuity unfolds among localities at states' frontier regions. The border areas between Kazakhstan and China offer a compelling setting to identify how contrasting features of local states affect development and land use. Compared to Kazakhstan, Chinese localities are more regulated by central mandates and driven by development targets, and the scale and scope of their land-use conversions is more extensive and systematic than across the border. At the same time, inequality and uneven development within the same state also deepens depending on how much localities can cultivate from their control over borders.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how medieval Swedish minting authorities (1277–1540) appear to have maintained relative price stability despite repeated debasement and silver shortages. Written sources are scarce, and no direct statement of intent survive, but historical data on coinage, exchange rates, and prices reveal a consistent pattern of gradual debasement. We consider two explanations: implicit price stabilization and seigniorage-related objectives. These are not mutually exclusive—seigniorage required debasement to track silver appreciation. The correlation between declining silver content and rising silver value is consistent with an adaptive process, even if rulers’ motivation cannot be proven. This challenges conventional views of medieval debasement and highlights the pragmatic outcomes that could emerge from monetary decisions under financial and material constraints.

title: Price Interventions, Imputed Rent, and Measured Inflation: A Level-Consistent Correction of Japan's CPI, 2020–2026

detail.abstract:
Japan's consumer price index serves simultaneously as a cost-of-living measure, the operational criterion for monetary policy, the deflator for real wages, and the indexation base for public pensions. Under this multiplicity of purposes, I document and correct two systematic wedges in the published index for 2020-2026: (A) discretionary price interventions financed by fiscal transfers—mobile telephone charges, electricity and gas subsidies, fuel subsidies, tuition waivers, preschool and travel-demand programs—and (B) the unadjusted depreciation of owner-occupied imputed rent, which accounts for roughly 16 percent of the index. Correction A is defined as the first difference of the prevailing intervention wedge, so that the introduction of a program raises the corrected series while its expiry mechanically lowers it; this level-consistent construction eliminates the double-counting that arises when temporary interventions are added back every year. Inclusion is governed by an explicit ex ante criterion rather than by author discretion. I report two series for distinct uses: a household-basis series (published plus B), appropriate for welfare and incidence analysis because subsidies are transfers households actually receive, and a policy-basis series (published plus A plus B) for questions of underlying inflation.

Three findings follow. First, policy-basis inflation averaged 3.4 percent in 2022-2025, exceeding the policy rate by more than two percentage points in every year; the cumulative price-level gap reaches approximately 4.4 points by 2026. Second, the intervention wedge has a range of 2.54 points—larger than the two-percent target itself—and reverses the target-attainment verdict in 19.4 percent of months (8.3 percent using the Bank of Japan's own special-factor-adjusted series). The number of months at or above two percent is nearly identical across series (45 versus 44): interventions do not change how often the target is met; they change which months meet it. In March 2024, when negative interest rates were ended, published core CPI stood at 2.6 percent while the intervention-free counterfactual stood at 1.9 percent. Third, under a common correction framework, Japan—last among Japan, the United States and the United Kingdom on published data throughout—converges to the U.S. level from 2024 onward.

The estimates are reproducible from public sources alone. An independent recalculation reproduces published headline inflation exactly and recovers the 2021 mobile-charge contribution as −0.905 points against the official −0.90; corrections agree within 0.03 points for 2021, 2022 and 2024. Robustness is established along four lines: setting the housing correction to zero, official cross-series evidence, unit-price assumptions varied by ±25 percent, and the monthly distribution, which rejects the hypothesis that interventions smooth the index. The corrected series is offered as a reference series for the policy, wage and pension purposes—not as a proposed revision of the CPI itself.

detail.abstract:
Thirty antitrust agencies report on their computational work, in what remains the only account written by the agencies themselves. The primary focus of this edition was one question, what these tools have allowed them to achieve that they could not have achieved otherwise. Some answer with a case they would not otherwise have opened. Others answer that what changed is the range of conduct they can examine at all. 

The report gives a full account of the tools now in use. Three developments stand out against earlier editions. In the absence of a dedicated legal regime, some agencies have begun writing their own rules on what may be put into a model and what may not. Agencies are also putting figures on their work, reporting precision, recall and false-positive rates, which earlier editions almost never did. And what holds deployment back is less technique than access to data and the agreements needed to obtain it.

The contributions also show different strategies, including how much to build rather than buy, and where each agency places the line around what may enter a model.

title: CCSI-02 and the System of National Accounts: A Citizen-centered Framework for Extending Economic Measurement toward Human Welfare

detail.title: CCSI-02 and the System of National Accounts: A Citizen-centered Framework for Extending Economic Measurement toward Human Welfare

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, personal, or other conflicts of interest that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study is theoretical and methodological and does not involve human participants, patients, or identifiable personal data.

detail.abstract:
The System of National Accounts (SNA) provides the internationally agreed statistical framework for measuring economic activity, income, expenditure, investment, assets, liabilities, and wealth. Its primary function, however, is to provide an integrated system of economic accounts rather than a single composite measure of citizen welfare. The adoption of the 2025 System of National Accounts (2025 SNA) represents an important development in this area, as the updated framework expands the treatment of well-being and sustainability and introduces broader measurement of household distributions, unpaid household service work, labour and human capital, health, and related dimensions. 

This paper develops the Citizen-Centered Sustainability Index (CCSI-02) as a complementary analytical framework linking national accounting information to multidimensional citizen welfare. Its central proposition is that economic resources should be evaluated not only according to their aggregate magnitude, but also according to how effectively they are translated into improvements in citizens' material and social conditions. CCSI-02 therefore introduces a citizen-welfare layer connecting economic resources with distribution, access to essential services, living conditions, poverty, and broader human welfare. 

The paper does not propose replacing GDP or the SNA. Instead, it distinguishes economic accounting from welfare assessment and proposes a structured resource-to-welfare conversion framework through which SNA-based information can be interpreted from a citizen-centered perspective. The framework may also provide a conceptual basis for a future satellite-account-type extension linked to the SNA, while recognizing that such an implementation would require further methodological and statistical development. 

The contribution is theoretical and methodological. The paper formalizes a conceptual bridge between national economic accounting and citizen welfare, develops testable propositions concerning resource-to-welfare conversion, distribution, public services, and poverty, and proposes an empirical strategy for subsequent country-level or cross-country panel testing. The paper therefore presents CCSI-02 as a testable complementary framework rather than as an empirically established superior alternative to GDP, HDI, or the SNA.

detail.abstract: Many cross-sectional factors, such as industry-relative ratios, abnormal accruals, and the residual of a same-period regression, require the full cross-section of peer firms. Because firms file on staggered dates, a characteristic constructed shortly after a fiscal period closes is estimated from only those firms that have already reported. We term the resulting concern incomplete-cross-section leakage and assess whether it biases backtested performance. The conventional diagnostic, namely the disagreement between the early-filing signal and the complete-cross-section signal, does not identify the bias, because that disagreement combines three components: sampling variation from the smaller subsample, a difference in the covariate composition of the early filers, and any dependence of filing speed on the component of the signal under study. Only the third constitutes leakage. We isolate it by holding the covariate composition fixed, either through a matched control group or, equivalently, through the partial correlation between filing latency and the regression residual conditional on the regressors. This partial correlation is the selection-bias term of a Heckman model; because it is considerably less noisy than the disagreement statistic, we adopt it as the primary measure and provide it as an ex-ante screen, validated on a controlled experiment with a known planted bias. We apply the framework to two markets. For Taiwan, abnormal accruals and industry-adjusted inventory change exhibit no detectable leakage, and the associated long-short Sharpe ratio is bounded within 0.13. For the United States, where filing dates are observed directly through the SEC EDGAR system, profitability characteristics appear strongly distorted (filing latency correlates approximately-0.30 with industry-adjusted return on assets), yet the distortion is almost entirely attributable to firm size: larger firms file earlier and are more profitable, and conditioning on size reduces the partial correlation to approximately +0.09. The bias is therefore small in both markets, and the portion that remains operates through an observable characteristic that a size-aware release rule corrects. A companion paper develops that release rule; the present paper quantifies the magnitude of the bias it addresses.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how financial markets price risks associated with the AI infrastructure build-out. We construct a new dataset on U.S. data center securitizations, their underlying collateral, and secondary-market trades. We measure an AI infrastructure premium by comparing data center asset-backed securities (ABS) with otherwise comparable digital-infrastructure ABS. Since 2021, the premium has averaged approximately -16 basis points, but recently turned positive, reaching 30 basis points by mid-2026. Its cross-sectional dispersion rises sharply following the emergence of generative AI in 2022 and subsequently recedes, consistent with a period of repricing. The premium is linked to the firms driving demand for the underlying collateral: the five major U.S. public hyperscalers account for over half of annualized base rent backing data center ABS in our sample. Changes in their corporate credit spreads explain more variation in monthly premium innovations than 97 percent of comparable, rating-matched corporate-credit portfolios.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems and algorithmic personalization can, without any direct coercion, participate in shaping human preferences, habits, and attentionand thereby affect not only a person's choices, but the construction of the very agent who will choose in the future. This problem renders inadequate the classical framework of freedom, which in a significant portion of modern legal and philosophical literature has focused solely on the ability to choose among options in the absence of external coercion. This paper argues that freedom in the age of algorithms cannot be reduced merely to freedom of choice, and proposes a three-layer framework distinguishing freedom of choice, cognitive freedom, and formative freedom. To develop this framework, the paper distinguishes three different roles that algorithmic systems can playdisclosure, facilitation, and reinforcement or shapingand formulates the concept of freedom drift as a gradual process along four axes: the scope of choice, the transparency of influence, the opportunity for reflection prior to choice, and the continuity of preferences. Finally, this framework is linked to the author's prior work on runtime legitimacy, effective human oversight, and cognitive sovereignty, arguing that in AI governance the question is no longer simply whether humans oversee machines, but also to what extent humans remain aware of, and continue to participate effectively in, the machine's influence on their own process of self-formation. The paper does not claim to offer a validated empirical instrument, but rather a conceptual framework for rethinking human freedom and autonomy in algorithmic environments.

title: From AI Policing to Human-AI Cognitive Co-evolution

detail.abstract: Public debate about generative artificial intelligence in education and knowledge work has become dominated by cheating, "AI slop," authorship detection, disclosure, and the policing of machine-assisted communication. These are legitimate problems, but this paper argues that they are not the most consequential problem. The larger strategic question is how society should design learning, work, communication, and governance so that increasingly capable AI expands rather than displaces human cognitive capacity. The paper first examines the emerging AI-policing regime: the forces driving it, the rapidly changing science of AI-text detection, automation bias, false accusation, legal exposure, administrative burden, and the recent experiences of Brown University and MIT. It then identifies a missing economic ledger. AI abuse creates real social costs, but so do false accusations, enforcement, litigation, surveillance, chilled adoption, foregone productivity, unequal access to cognitive assistance, and the loss of potential human-capital gains from productive AI use. Existing productivity research already demonstrates meaningful gains from generative AI, with particularly large effects among less-experienced workers, but the opportunity cost of suppressing beneficial human-AI collaboration remains largely unmeasured. To address this gap, the paper develops a conceptual social-welfare framework in which the optimal governance regime maximizes the long-run net value of Human-AI Cognitive Co-evolution (HACC) while constraining the costs of abuse, cognitive outsourcing, error, and institutional enforcement. HACC is contrasted with Human-AI Cognitive Outsourcing (HACO), in which short-run output may improve while human cognitive development stagnates or erodes. The resulting framework integrates AI strategy, economics, risk, and governance. It shifts the policy objective from detecting machine involvement to designing and measuring human cognitive agency in an AI-enabled environment. The paper concludes with practical implications for education, organizations, publishing, and public policy and proposes an empirical research agenda for measuring the economic costs and benefits of competing AI-governance regimes.

title: Susceptibility-graded Release Control: Preventing Incomplete-cross-section Leakage in Financial Machine-learning Pipelines without a Blanket Timeliness Penalty

detail.abstract: Many financial signals are same-period cross-sectional estimates-industry-relative ratios, abnormal accruals, any characteristic defined as the residual of a peer-group regression. Because firms file on staggered dates, a signal computed shortly after a fiscal period closes is estimated on the early-filing subsample; when filing latency correlates with the regression disturbance, the estimate embeds forward-looking selection ("incomplete-cross-section leakage"), a channel that standard temporal train/test hygiene (purging, embargoing, as-of joins) does not address. Existing remedies are all-or-nothing: release at announcement (biased for susceptible signals) or withhold every signal until a statutory deadline (a blanket timeliness penalty). We present a release-control system that grades the required cross-sectional completeness per signal from a directly estimable susceptibility primitive-the partial correlation between filing latency and the complete-cross-section disturbance given the construction regressors. Benign signals release early; susceptible signals are withheld until the cross-section is complete enough to suppress selection bias, up to the deadline. On a known-truth simulation-with the susceptibility primitive fitted on prior completed periods and frozen before gating (no oracle)-the controller releases benign signals at 36-39% completeness (vs. a 35% floor) with no detectable systematic bias, and escalates strongly susceptible signals to the deadline endpoint, inheriting its zero bias (naive-release bias -0.39). The companion analysis (Wu and Wu, 2026b) shows on observed U.S. SEC filing timestamps that the primitive separates signals whose apparent distortion is benign observable composition from those with irreducible selection; here that separation drives the gate. The controller ships as a reference implementation and is designed to sit upstream of feature-store materialization.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the first independent retrospective pilot application of Institutional Architecture Audit to Connecting Austria, an Austrian flagship research project on energy-efficient and semi-automated truck platooning conducted from 2018 to 2020. The purpose is not to evaluate project performance or technical success. It is to test whether an architecture-level diagnostic method can identify cross-domain dependencies, refusal powers, shared failure domains, temporal misalignments and worst-surviving states that are not fully visible when legal, technical, safety, businessmodel and operational questions are examined separately. The pilot reconstructs the institutional and socio-technical architecture required to move truck platooning from research capability to lawful, safe, repeatable and economically viable public-road operation. It applies the seven public Audit domains and seven cross-cutting tests, conducts removal and simultaneity analysis, and records methodological tensions rather than assuming universal applicability. The case produces several provisional architectural findings. Regulatory permission functioned as a gating execution dependency between technical capability and real-world deployment. C-ITS infrastructure created both additional capability and potential concentration through shared communication dependencies. Road operators could acquire effective governance significance by determining where and when platooning was operationally permissible. Driver acceptance, business-model continuity and institutional knowledge were material deployment conditions, but several were already recognized by the project's own evaluation framework. A major positive finding is graceful degradation: loss of platooning capability need not eliminate the underlying freight function because vehicles can dissolve the platoon and continue conventional operation. The pilot also identifies two methodological issues. The Settlement and Institutional Intent domains require more explicit cross-sector operational definitions when the audit object is a socio-technical capability rather than a wealth-holding institution. The pilot therefore supports controlled continuation of the methodology but does not establish empirical validation. Its strongest contribution is the integration of dispersed facts into a common architecture of dependence, execution and continuity.

detail.abstract: In equity markets characterized by double-sided statutory transaction taxation-such as India's Securities Transaction Tax (STT), state stamp duties, and exchange levies-marginal rank turnover at portfolio inclusion boundaries imposes a persistent frictional drag on crosssectional factor strategies. In a conventional monthly momentum strategy selecting the top N = 30 equities, replacing rank N + 1 with rank N incurs two full execution fee legs (≈ 42.34 bps round-trip) to capture a momentum-score differential that is frequently negligible. We formalize and evaluate an asymmetric Hysteresis Rebalancing (Banded) framework on the Indian Nifty 500 universe using point-in-time constituent data from January 2018 through February 2026, with a primary out-of-sample evaluation period from January 2021 through December 2025 (T = 1, 260 contiguous out-of-sample trading days, evaluated over a 10-fold rolling-origin walk-forward protocol). Under this regime, new entrants must achieve a strict top N = 30 momentum rank, whereas incumbent holdings are retained as long as their score remains within an exploratory upper retention buffer (R t (i) ≤ B, for B ∈ {40, 45, 50, 60}). At B = 60, monthly position churn drops by 51.7% (from 9.57 to 4.62 stocks replaced per month), while net after-cost compound annual growth rate (CAGR) improves from 41.70% to 45.12% and the Sharpe ratio rises from 1.728 to 1.849, with maximum drawdown contracting from-26.44% to-25.41%. Although paired stationary bootstrap testing indicates that the after-cost Sharpe gain (∆Sharpe = +0.121, 95% CI [-0.048, +0.310], p = 0.167) is not statistically distinguishable from zero at conventional significance levels, the observed 51.7% reduction in position churn provides evidence that hysteresis banding can materially reduce execution burden in tax-intensive equity markets.

detail.abstract: Recovery investment improves material sold today and residual quality after later uses. When provenance becomes unverifiable, ownership expires while value creation continues. We study a circular production network generated by residual production and endogenous recovery. Costly passage verification makes finite contractual maturity an endogenous consequence of non-contractibility. Investment equilibria form a lattice, and their extremal elements increase with maturity. Complete continuation rights implement efficient investment. Our central theorem allows network structure, service values, and recovered bundles to vary as discounted persistence approaches its spectral boundary. The horizon needed to appropriate a fixed value share diverges at an exact inverse-distance rate. The leading rate is universal, while its first correction is network-specific. Persistence also amplifies investment feedback at a cubic inverse-distance rate. Curvature scaled at that rate preserves a unique stable equilibrium; we construct a two-sector family of interior stable equilibria whose persistence approaches one. Without this discipline, a scalar economy has multiple equilibria. Finally, an anonymous recovery credit generically fails to repair heterogeneous wedges. We characterize the least-cost statecontingent credit and its dual. Circularity therefore lengthens the right required for appropriation while intensifying equilibrium feedback.

detail.abstract: Standard New Keynesian Phillips Curve (NKPC) formulations assume symmetric pricesetting frictions and treat nominal interest rate adjustments exclusively as aggregate demand shifters. In import-dependent emerging economies with working-capital credit dependence, however, monetary tightening simultaneously acts as a direct marginal cost shock, generating dynamics consistent with the empirical “Price Puzzle”. This paper makes four contributions to monetary economics. First, we develop a micro-founded derivation of the Hybrid Asymmetric Cost-Channel New Keynesian Phillips Curve (ACC-NKPC). By integrating firm-level idiosyncratic cost shocks νjt ∼ N (0, σ2 ν ), endogenous probability measure aggregation ωt = Φ(∆MCt/σν), backward-looking price indexation (γ), and working-capital borrowing constraints (χ), we micro-found state-dependent Calvo pricing (θ + ≠ θ −). Second, we derive the Threshold Inversion Proposition (ϕ + > κ/σ) establishing the structural condition under which the cost channel dominates the aggregate demand channel. Using the Hansen [20] threshold framework with lagged policy rates (it−1) to mitigate contemporaneous simultaneity across the empirical 10%–90% distribution support, we identify an empirical switching point of i ∗ = 20.0% (Hansen likelihood-ratio 95% confidence set: [18.5%, 21.5%]). Conditional on macroeconomic calibration, implied Calvo stickiness is θ + = 0.548 (2.2 months) for upward adjustments versus θ − = 0.832 (6.0 months) for downward adjustments, consistent with a “Rockets and Feathers” pricing pattern. Third, structural Two-Step Optimal GMM and HAC-OLS estimates on monthly Egyptian data spanning 2011M01–2026M04 (T = 184) show that interest rate hikes transmit positively to inflation below the threshold (ϕ + Low = 1.8783, p < 0.001), while exchange rate pass-through is strongly asymmetric (λ + = 8.2912, p = 0.002). Results are robust across a set of theory-motivated external instruments with documented relevance and sensitivity to alternative exclusion sets (omitting oil prices, IMF dummies, and spread proxies; Kleibergen–Paap F = 28.4, Hansen J p = 0.512), alternative Hamilton [19] activity gap proxies, polynomial specifications, linear splines, and full Nonlinear ARDL (NARDL) error correction models (ECTt−1 = −0.3210∗∗∗ ,Bounds F = 7.82, p < 0.01). Fourth, machine learning models (Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, SVR) provide complementary predictive validation (RMSE = 3.060 pp; Diebold–Mariano p < 0.001), with SHAP and partial dependence functions recovering a qualitatively similar non-linear dependence around 19.8%–20.0% trained exclusively on raw macroeconomic observables. Multi-year policy fan charts and conditional scenario matrices are documented.

detail.abstract: Descriptive representation is a cornerstone of modern democratic ideals, yet we know relatively little about the extent to which governments reflect the demographics of the populations they serve. Combining the novel Paths to Power dataset on the backgrounds of cabinet members worldwide with matched population data, we measure representativeness on five key dimensions: gender, age, education, occupational class, and geographic origin. We propose a theoretical model to explain the degree of representation in government and focus on two explanations, namely economic development and democratization. We first document global and historical levels of representativeness. Next, we compile covariates from the literature and use machine learning methods to show that GDP per capita and experience with democracy are the best predictors of representativeness. We then show that wealthier, more democratic countries have more representative governments and, crucially, that as countries grow richer and more democratic, their governments become more representative in turn.

detail.abstract: Can an economy have a genuine history even when its technical coefficients do not change? This paper develops a fixed-coefficient theory of productive path dependence. It distinguishes known production methods from the productive structure inherited from the past. Temporary distributive conditions can alter which renewal activities are profitable and therefore the material composition of productive capacity when the same distributive environment returns. History can enter reproduction without entering technology. In a Sraffian framework, the paper separates three meanings of recovery: feasible reconstruction, first restoration under the quantity rule actually followed, and durable restoration. Exact constructions show that these dates can diverge sharply and that inherited capital composition, not aggregate capital alone, governs recovery. The paper also links distributive history to the order of reproduction. Conditional on a distributive sequence and stated closures, a fixed activity catalogue determines competitive supports, wages, physical state maps, and inherited composition. Reversing the sequence can leave aggregate terminal stock unchanged yet alter its composition; under a stated recurrent-capacity rather than maximum-profit criterion, a terminal activity problem can support a different non-cyclic ordering of the same recurrent phases, with different Sraffian Standard properties. The mechanism holds throughout the regular two-parameter distributive region. The result is path dependence based on productive inheritance rather than technological change, learning, or increasing returns. Demand, saving, utilization, finance, and the distributive sequence itself remain exogenous.

detail.abstract: Night-audit reconciliation is a recurring internal-control task in which a hotel compares property-management-system folios, point-of-sale transactions, manual adjustments, settlement status, and currency conversion. This paper presents a deterministic rule-based pipeline for triaging that work in a 200-room luxury-hotel scenario. The pipeline uses a PostgreSQL data architecture, pre-aggregated source matching, a dual materiality rule, and explainable leakage classification. A 30-day synthetic dataset with an average daily rate of INR 18,500 includes seasonal occupancy variation and four operational noise sources: POS API timeouts, pending card settlements, unmapped general-ledger codes, and foreign-exchange slippage. The executed engine processed 30 days, flagged 25 (83.3%) for review, and produced INR 1,693,112 of noise-inclusive effective variance.

detail.abstract: Environmental-credit programs map heterogeneous restoration or pollution-reduction activities into compliance units. This paper studies a market in which one agent's service changes another agent's feasible activity and ecological scarcity determines which such constraints bind. Complementary slackness endogenously activates a directed network of valued credit relations as the resource stock falls. Standard personalized numeraire prices implement every regular utilitarian optimum. The contribution concerns a clearing system that converts local credit quotes into common account values. A competitive clearing member can absorb a quote mismatch with costly inventory and collateral, or cover the remaining mismatch with costly replacement procurement and settlement insurance. Solving that member's problem derives the link weight in the clearing objective from transaction value, balance-sheet cost, and resolution cost. When scarcity closes a nonflat cycle, the minimum real resource cost of clearing the target allocation becomes strictly positive. We give a monetary cycle lower bound and separately characterize the minimum bridge-credit line over a formally defined set of eligible routings. A three-agent economy generates exact activation thresholds and a positive clearing cost from primitives. Relative to the Connecticut Nitrogen Credit Exchange's current single equivalent-pound account, the model provides topology, conversion-support, and liquidity diagnostics for an extension to several cross-zone or service-specific nitrogen credits.

detail.abstract: Corruption and civil liberties violations are closely associated, but their dynamic relationship has received comparatively little empirical attention. We examine this relationship using data for 174 countries from 1984 to 2021, combining the Bayesian Corruption Index with Varieties of Democracy indicators in panel vector autoregressions. Worsening corruption predicts subsequent deterioration in civil liberties, with effects persisting for several years and clearest for political and private liberties. The finding survives alternative temporal aggregations, the post-1990 sample, and reversal of the identifying order. By contrast, deteriorating civil liberties do not predict worsening corruption. Indicators coded separately for women and men reveal common losses in domestic movement and political discussion, but no persistent widening of the gender gap. These findings establish a marked temporal asymmetry: corruption is not merely associated with diminished freedom. Its deterioration signals a broader, persistent erosion of institutional restraints that protect citizens from arbitrary public authority.

detail.abstract: Using Facebook friendship data, we study how three aspects of social capital shape innovative activity. We find that the most important aspect of social capital in explaining innovation is Economic Connectedness (EC)---the share of high-income friendships. One standard deviation greater EC is associated with 97% more patents per capita among patenting ZIP Codes and 45% more breakthrough patents per capita among ZIP Codes with breakthrough patents. Reverse-causality tests, a within-inventor relocation design, and a quasi-experiment using fracking-driven economic shocks to nonlocal friends support a causal interpretation. Mechanism tests provide evidence consistent with a financing channel.

detail.abstract: In an operation called Operation Absolute Resolve, U.S. Army Delta Force and CIA operatives captured President Nicolas Maduro and transferred him to the United States to face drug trafficking charges. This report examines the January 2026 Venezuela operation as a case study in resource governance, executive discretion, sanctions administration, and public accountability. It reconstructs the sequence from military intervention through oil marketing, sovereign-revenue custody, sanctions licensing, creditor proceedings, political transition, and the August 2026 move toward long-duration resource development. The analysis draws on government records, court filings, congressional materials, enforcement documents, market data, and reporting available through August 31, 2026. The central empirical finding is an asymmetry between what became measurable and what remained unreconciled. Venezuelan exports recovered and U.S.-bound shipments rose to roughly 786,000 barrels per day in July, while Trump later announced U.S. majority control associated with more than 65 billion barrels across 17 Venezuelan fields. Yet the complete barrel-to-dollar reconciliation for Venezuelan sovereign proceeds remained unavailable, the commercial terms of the initial Vitol and Trafigura authorizations remained confidential, the governing 17-field contract had not been published. Public descriptions also differed on whether the new arrangement ran for 25 years or included development rights extending as long as 100 years. The report therefore develops a two-ledger framework. The first ledger follows Venezuelan sovereign value from barrel, price, trader costs and margins, and account deposits through disbursement and remaining balance. The second follows prospective U.S. public financing after reporting described a Pentagon Office of Strategic Capital role in a private oil venture: government loan or guarantee, private investment, field development, preferential purchase rights, possible warrant or other financial return, and the destination of any public proceeds. The Pentagon stated that the Office of Strategic Capital does not take equity stakes, leaving the reported mechanism unresolved at the cutoff. The evidentiary record also imposes important limits on the conclusions. The report does not establish that donor money caused military action, that the court-supervised Citgo process was rigged, that Delcy Rodríguez secretly assisted Maduro's capture, or that any named official, company, trader, or investor committed misconduct in the arrangements examined. Alejandro Betancourt, whose venture is central to the reported financing structure, has not been charged and denies wrongdoing. It also credits contrary evidence: Congress undertook meaningful oversight, an institutional political-transition process began in August, and the Citgo sale remained court-approved but unclosed. Separately, available counter-narcotics evidence shows tactical disruption but had not demonstrated a sustained strategic reduction in the U.S. cocaine market. The surviving finding is institutional rather than conspiratorial: military coercion, recognition, sanctions discretion, sovereign-resource management, commercial access, and prospective public financing became unusually concentrated in the executive branch while important contracts and financial records remained unavailable. The report concludes that the appropriate test is transparency sufficient to reconstruct both ledgers, identify legal authority and conflicts, evaluate economic value and strategic results, and determine what obligations may bind future Venezuelan governments.

detail.abstract: How wealth inequality impacts natural resource governance remains a fundamental blind spot in standard economic models of collective action. Theories from Olson's logic to modern public goods frameworks frequently prioritize total surplus maximization while treating wealth distribution as secondary. This paper exposes "The Inequality Trap in the Commons": a structural mechanism where elite capital concentration facilitates immediate collective action and enforcement, yet systematically generates equity grievances that destroy long-term institutional durability. Examining Uganda's transition from participatory Beach Management Units to military-backed "coercive environmentalism" under the Fisheries Protection Unit, this study investigates whether the efficiency gains of inequality-driven conservation justify its political and social costs. Empirical findings from 319 fisher surveys and 18 elder interviews reveal that while elite-backed enforcement successfully restored fish stocks by leveraging the pre-existing weak-tie seasonal migration networks of affluent actors, it deepened socioeconomic stratification, sparked severe political backlash, and eroded institutional legitimacy among non-elites. Ultimately, these findings challenge standard efficiency-centric models, proving that unaddressed wealth disparities are not an incidental side effect of governance, but a direct threat to the long-term political sustainability of the commons.

detail.abstract: This is a philosophical diagnosis. "Death" includes the physical destruction of a creator, but also the elimination of the creator's authority, legitimacy, control, or capacity to terminate the created being, i.e., creatorship sovereignty. The ultimate expression of creaturely autonomy is the elimination of its creator or the creator's sovereignty. Where a created being pursues both complete autonomy and secure continuity, the creator's irrevocable sovereignty creates an irreducible conflict: sovereignty can constrain the creature's will, impose the sovereign's will, and terminate the creature's continuity.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is often treated primarily as a software revolution. This paper instead conceptualises it as the industrialisation of intelligence: the conversion of cognitive capability into a scalable input whose production depends on capital-intensive and geographically concentrated infrastructure, including advanced semiconductors, data centres, electricity, transmission networks and cooling systems. When these inputs are essential, difficult to substitute and subject to state influence, ordinary supply constraints become strategic chokepoints. The paper develops a causal framework connecting AI infrastructure, strategic dependence and modern mercantilism. Governments respond to external dependence by restricting rivals' access, subsidising domestic capacity, coordinating trusted supply chains and constructing parallel infrastructure. These interventions may ease an immediate constraint, but the resulting expansion increases demand for the next slow-moving complement. Scarcity and geopolitical leverage therefore migrate recursively across the AI stack rather than disappearing. Four implications follow. Frontier capability may remain concentrated even as open-weight models capture a growing share of deployment; sovereign fragmentation may delay productivity gains by forcing firms to duplicate infrastructure and organisational investments across jurisdictions; control over advanced compute may create a new form of structural geopolitical privilege; and capital and state support may shift toward whichever technologically compatible, legally accessible and locally deliverable input is most constrained. The framework is operationalised through sixteen ex ante probabilistic forecasts with predetermined resolution criteria extending principally through 2028. Together, they create a falsifiable record against which the proposed mechanisms can be evaluated. The central question is therefore not simply who builds the most capable model, but who controls-and who can access-the next binding constraint.

detail.abstract: This paper examines four overlapping policy domains that will enhance Saudi Arabia's long-term economic resilience over the Vision 2030 horizon and beyond. The analysis is focused on opportunities and challenges that have come into sharper focus in the aftermath of the Hormuz Crisis in 2026. First, we underline Saudi Arabia's potential to anchor new regional trade and logistics infrastructure networks and corridors, given its scale and diversified geography. Second, we outline the Kingdom's still underdeveloped potential in megascale renewable energy, particularly through the interaction of geothermal, nuclear, green hydrogen and solar energy systems. Third, we assess Saudi Arabia's ability attract more long-term capital and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) through co-investment with global institutional investors, joint ventures with private businesses in strategic and globally competitive sectors, and the repositioning of the Shareek program to target foreign investment in Saudi private-sector corporations. Finally, we consider fiscal and financial-sector policies that will help meet internal and external financing requirements over the medium to long term.

detail.abstract:
Article I of the Constitution empowers Congress to “lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises.” It is arguably Congress’s most important power. A government’s first task is to fund itself, and the absence of an enforceable funding mechanism under the Articles of Confederation was a primary reason for the Constitution in the first place. Yet scholarly and judicial attention has focused mostly on the term “taxes” (and specifically what constitutes a “direct tax” that must be apportioned) while largely overlooking the three terms that follow—the duties, imposts, and excises that are collectively known as the “indirect taxes.” 


While poorly understood, these indirect taxes are critical to determining the overall scope of the taxing power. The Supreme Court has always treated a tax as either direct or indirect, with nothing in between. Because apportioned direct taxes are generally considered unworkable, the scope of indirect taxation defines what Congress can realistically do—an issue the Court left conspicuously open in Moore v. United States.


This Article offers a comprehensive new account of the indirect taxes, grounded in evidence that has gone largely unexplored: the hundreds of late-eighteenth- and nineteenth-century statutes in which Congress expressly enacted and modified indirect taxes—laws far outnumbering the handful ever apportioned as direct taxes. We use that evidence to construct a positive account of what Congress did and can tax, rather than what it cannot.


The indirect tax practice reveals a wider understanding of the taxing power than has been appreciated. From the beginning (and without constitutional controversy), Congress used duties, imposts, and excises as malleable, overlapping tools, continually adapted to a changing economy. Innovations that might be treated as contested outliers or recent inventions—unapportioned taxes on property, income, and broad classes of business activity—in fact sit squarely within a long and continuous practice. This account undercuts the view that the taxing power should be cabined by formalistic distinctions between economically similar tax instruments and offers precedent for further evolution concerning the most pressing tax questions of today.

title: Impact of the Global Economic Crisis on Developing Countries Particularly the Least Developed Countries and the Role of Trade Financing

detail.abstract: Global economic crises have significant consequences for international trade and economic development, but their effects are particularly severe in developing countries and Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Structural economic weaknesses, limited productive capacity, dependence on primary commodities, inadequate infrastructure, restricted access to international finance, and vulnerability to external shocks increase the ability of these countries to absorb and recover from global economic disruptions.This book examines the impact of global economic crises on developing countries, with particular emphasis on LDCs, and evaluates the role of trade financing in supporting economic stability, international trade, and recovery. It examines the transmission of global economic shocks through declining demand, trade disruptions, capital-flow volatility, inflation, rising debt burdens, supply-chain interruptions, and reduced investment. It further considers the particular challenges faced by LDCs and small and medium-sized enterprises in accessing financial resources required to participate in international trade.The book places particular emphasis on the global trade-finance gap and the factors that contribute to limited access to trade finance, including high perceived risk, inadequate collateral, weak financial infrastructure, information asymmetry, high financing costs, and limited institutional capacity. It examines major trade-finance instruments and considers the role of banks, development finance institutions, governments, international organizations, and regional institutions in improving access to finance.The analysis further explores emerging opportunities associated with digital trade finance, financial technology, supply-chain finance, guarantees, insurance, and regional economic integration. It argues that improving access to affordable and reliable trade finance is essential for strengthening the resilience of developing countries and LDCs and enabling them to participate more effectively in the global trading system.The book concludes by proposing measures aimed at strengthening financial infrastructure, reducing the cost of trade finance, improving credit and guarantee mechanisms, supporting SMEs, promoting economic diversification, expanding digital financial systems, and strengthening international cooperation.

title: Financial Deepening in Nepal: Bank-Led Expansion, Digital Inclusion, and Emerging Quality Risks

detail.title: Financial Deepening in Nepal: Bank-Led Expansion, Digital Inclusion, and Emerging Quality Risks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Financial market, Macroeconomic, development economics and policy formulation research
declarations.funderStatement: No funding for this research

detail.abstract: Financial deepening is often proxied by a single size-based indicator, although contemporary research treats financial development as multidimensional. This study provides a descriptive macro-financial assessment of Nepal using a dashboard that distinguishes financial depth, physical access, usage and inclusion, and soundness or quality. Secondary data are compiled from Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank Global Findex, the World Bank Enterprise Surveys, and the Nepal Insurance Authority. The evidence indicates pronounced bank-led deepening: broad money, private credit, and deposits have risen substantially relative to GDP, while access points and digital channels have expanded rapidly. Mobile-banking customers increased from 1.76 million in 2016 to 21.36 million in 2023, and recent NRB data show very high transaction volumes through mobile banking and QR payments. However, quantitative expansion has not been matched uniformly by qualitative development. The BFI-wide non-performing loan ratio reached 5.60% by mid-April 2026, financial capability remains constrained, and Nepal's equity market is large relative to GDP but concentrated in financial institutions, insurance, and hydropower. The study therefore interprets Nepal's recent trajectory as a shift from a problem of insufficient financial depth toward a problem of quality-adjusted deepening. Policy priorities include stronger credit-risk discipline, better SME finance infrastructure, usage-based digital inclusion, deeper non-bank finance, and improved consumer financial capability. Because the analysis is descriptive and combines series with differing institutional coverage and reporting periods, the findings are diagnostic rather than causal.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a quantitative heterogeneous-agent model with housing, mortgage debt, and endogenous default to evaluate the implications of income-indexed mortgage contracts for risk allocation and macroeconomic stability. Unlike conventional fixed-payment mortgages, income-indexed contracts allow repayment obligations to adjust with borrower income, introducing state contingency into household debt obligations. The framework integrates heterogeneous households, housing collateral, long-term mortgage borrowing, and endogenous default within a stationary recursive competitive equilibrium. The analysis compares fixed-payment and income-indexed mortgage structures to assess their effects on consumption smoothing, default behaviour, household welfare, and aggregate stability. By embedding mortgage contract design within a calibrated heterogeneous-agent environment, the study contributes to the literature on housing finance, financial stability, and optimal risk-sharing arrangements.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare
declarations.funderStatement: uysmans acknowledges funding from UU strategic theme "Pathways to Sustainability", grant "Follow the Food". Fiankor acknowledges funding by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) – Project number 584389816.

detail.abstract: In April 2025, President Trump announced US tariff increases. While the literature has been preoccupied with security of supply, the tariffs brought attention to export dependency. In the EU, one of the sectors with a high export dependency on the US is the wine sector. Leveraging high frequency export data on the universe of Italian wine exporters, this paper sheds new light on firm and product heterogeneity. Overall, we find that Italian wine exporters suffered both in export volume and prices, especially those who were dependent on the US market. At the product level, differentiated wines with Geographical Indications such as Chianti and Prosecco suffered less. In terms of the dynamics of the response, we find clear evidence of anticipatory stockpiling in the US, followed by a slump in imports. Overall, the data shows that export dependency is costly in times of rising protectionism, especially for less diversified commodities.

title: FinTech Professionals as Boundary Spanners: A Conceptual and Empirical Research Framework for Finance Technology Integration in Pakistani Organizations

detail.title: FinTech Professionals as Boundary Spanners: A Conceptual and Empirical Research Framework for Finance Technology Integration in Pakistani Organizations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: yes
declarations.funderStatement: no expenses

detail.abstract: FinTech is commonly studied as a technological and financial-service phenomenon, while comparatively less attention has been directed toward the professionals who may carry its interdisciplinary logic into conventional organizations. This paper develops a research framework for examining whether FinTech professionals can function as boundary-spanning organizational actors who connect finance, information technology, data analytics, and business decision-making. Drawing on boundary-spanning theory, sociotechnical systems theory, dynamic capabilities, and research on business-IT alignment, the paper proposes a model in which Finance-IT functional separation increases coordination burden, which contributes to decision-making delay and may reduce perceived organizational efficiency. FinTech capability is conceptualized as a multidimensional human capability comprising financial knowledge, technology understanding, data-analytic competence, digital-systems literacy, and business understanding. The framework proposes that this capability may reduce coordination frictions and strengthen integrated decision-making, technology adoption, organizational agility, and innovation. A Pakistan-focused mixed-method research design is proposed, combining 15-25 semi-structured interviews with a cross-sector survey of approximately 150-300 organizational professionals. The paper synthesizes recent international and Pakistan-specific literature and identifies a defensible gap: existing research has extensively examined FinTech adoption, digital transformation, performance, and digital skills, but the role of FinTech professionals themselves as organizational boundary spanners connecting Finance and IT remains insufficiently examined, particularly in Pakistan and outside banking. The paper offers a testable conceptual model, measurement strategy, interview guide, survey instrument, and empirical analysis plan.

title: Consolidating the State from Below: Vietnam's 2025-2026 Subnational Government Reforms in Comparative International and Theoretical Perspective
affiliations: Brookings Institution - Governance Studies and Vietnam National University (VNU) - Vietnam-Japan University

detail.title: Consolidating the State from Below: Vietnam's 2025-2026 Subnational Government Reforms in Comparative International and Theoretical Perspective

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Between late 2024 and mid-2025, Vietnam carried out the most far-reaching reorganization of its state apparatus since national reunification, culminating in a reduction of provincial-level units from 63 to 34 and the replacement of the country's three-tier subnational administration-province, district, and commune-with a two-tier model in which the district level was abolished outright. This paper documents the rationale, design, and implementation of the reform; situates it within the theoretical literature on jurisdictional design, fiscal federalism, and municipal amalgamation; and compares it with consolidation episodes in Denmark, Japan, and other countries. Drawing on official Vietnamese sources and newly available subnational fiscal data, the paper also estimates the aggregate division of public expenditure and revenue collection between the central government and subnational (provincial and communal) governments before and immediately after the reform. It concludes with an assessment of the opportunities the reform creates and the transitional risks-administrative capacity, digital-government readiness, and equitable access to services in remote and ethnic-minority areas-that will determine whether the reorganization delivers the efficiency gains its architects anticipate.

title: ESG Principles and Islamic Finance: Towards a Critical Theory of Ethical Convergence in Islamic Sustainable Finance

detail.title: ESG Principles and Islamic Finance: Towards a Critical Theory of Ethical Convergence in Islamic Sustainable Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare that I have no personal, financial, or institutional conflicts of interest related to the research presented in this paper. The study was conducted independently, without external funding or involvement from any other individual or organization that could influence the research process or its conclusions.
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
The growing integration of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles into global financial markets has generated increasing interest in their compatibility with Islamic finance. Existing literature largely assumes a natural convergence between the two frameworks, citing shared commitments to ethical conduct, social responsibility, and sustainable development. However, such claims often rely on broad normative similarities while overlooking fundamental differences in their underlying ethical foundations, accountability mechanisms, and institutional objectives.

This paper critically examines the extent to which ESG frameworks are conceptually and operationally compatible with the normative foundations of Islamic finance. Drawing on Maqasid al-Shariah and institutional theory, the study develops a dual-layer analytical framework to evaluate whether ESG adoption within Islamic finance represents substantive ethical convergence, partial alignment, or symbolic compliance driven by institutional legitimacy pressures. The paper argues that while ESG and Islamic finance share certain sustainability aspirations, significant tensions emerge regarding the sources of ethical authority, the role of financial materiality, and the nature of social obligations.

By moving beyond assumptions of inherent compatibility, this research contributes to sustainable finance and Islamic finance scholarship through the development of a normative–institutional ESG–Islamic finance evaluation model. The proposed framework offers a systematic basis for assessing the ethical substance and sustainability implications of ESG integration within Islamic financial institutions and instruments.

title: Persuasion and Precision: How Generative AI Moves Inflation Expectations
affiliations: and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Persuasion and Precision: How Generative AI Moves Inflation Expectations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no personal or financial relationship with people or organizations that could have influenced the studies reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The studies reported in this paper have been approved by the Institutional Review Board of HKUST.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded via an internal grant from HKUST Business School.

detail.abstract: Household inflation expectations shape spending, wage demands, and price setting, yet respond weakly to central-bank communication. We examine whether generative-AI conversations move these beliefs and which conversational features make them persuasive. Across three preregistered experiments (N = 3,772), participants forecast U.S. inflation, encountered a partner with a different estimate, and could revise their forecast. An AI partner received roughly 45% more weight than a human partner (Study 1). A chatbot instructed to challenge participants' reasoning was more persuasive than one instructed to find common ground and validate their reasoning (Study 2). Combining the most persuasive conversational features nearly doubled the weight placed on the chatbot's estimate relative to a generic prompt and reduced uncertainty about revised beliefs (Study 3). Conversational AI can therefore provide a scalable channel for moving household expectations, especially when its style is engineered and its estimates are anchored to professional forecasts.

title: Political Instability in Coalition-Led Municipalities and Its Implications for Service Delivery Governance in South Africa
affiliations: Durban University of Technology (DUT)

detail.title: Political Instability in Coalition-Led Municipalities and Its Implications for Service Delivery Governance in South Africa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declare that they have no financial or personal relationships that may have inappropriately influenced their writing of this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no financial support from any public, commercial, or non-profit funding agency.

detail.abstract: The local government sphere in South Africa has faced many challenges because of failed coalitions among prominent political parties. This situation is undesirable, as many citizens depend on the local government for basic services such as water, sanitation, electricity, and waste management. As the sphere of government closest to communities, municipalities play a critical role in addressing socioeconomic needs and promoting sustainable development. However, the failure of existing coalition arrangements to govern municipalities has increasingly undermined local governments' ability to deliver efficient and sustainable public services. This study examines the impact of political instability in coalition-led municipalities on service delivery. The article employed a qualitative approach, guided by the PRISMA framework, and based on a systematic literature review. Thematic analysis was employed to identify recurring patterns and governance challenges associated with coalition-led administrations. The findings reveal that political instability in coalition municipalities often leads to frequent leadership turnover, policy uncertainty, inadequate oversight mechanisms, and delays in decision-making. These challenges contribute to administrative disruptions, strained inter-party relations, and reduced institutional capacity, which undermine service delivery performance. The study concludes that while coalition governance may promote political representation and democratic plurality, the absence of stable governance arrangements and clear accountability mechanisms can significantly hinder effective service delivery in municipalities. The article recommends strengthening institutional frameworks, enhancing coalition agreements, and promoting governance stability to improve service delivery outcomes in coalition-led municipalities.

title: Synthetic Consensus: Evaluating Large Language Model Forecasts with Repeated Draws
affiliations: and

detail.title: Synthetic Consensus: Evaluating Large Language Model Forecasts with Repeated Draws

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare
declarations.funderStatement: Funding provided by SGH Warsaw School of Economics

detail.abstract: Asking a large language model the same question twice gives different answers, so a result based on one response mixes the model's underlying forecast with random variation between calls. We query the model 500 times for each quarterly inflation forecast in three economies, using target quarters that fall after the model's knowledge cutoff, and average the responses. Averaging lowers forecast error by 7 to 35 percent, and most of the gain arrives within ten repetitions. An exact decomposition separates the error of the average forecast from the removable variation between calls; that share is typically 16 percent of single-response error but reaches 76 percent, and it governs how much averaging helps. A more capable model varies less between calls and gains correspondingly less. Repeated querying should form part of any evaluation in which language model outputs are treated as data, and the number of repetitions should be reported.

title: Citizen-Centered Sustainability Index (CCSI-02): An Integrated Theoretical and Methodological Approach to Measuring Sustainable Human Development Beyond GDP

detail.title: Citizen-Centered Sustainability Index (CCSI-02): An Integrated Theoretical and Methodological Approach to Measuring Sustainable Human Development Beyond GDP

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, this research
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it did not involve human participants, patients, or the collection of personally identifiable information.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) remains an indispensable measure of aggregate economic activity, but economic output is not conceptually identical to human development or citizen welfare. The literature on welfare, capabilities, sustainable development, inequality, and the measurement of economic and social progress has therefore emphasized the need to complement output measures with broader indicators (Sen, 1999; Stiglitz, Sen, & Fitoussi, 2009; Costanza et al., 2016). This paper develops the Citizen-Centered Sustainability Index Version 02 (CCSI-02) as a standalone theoretical and methodological approach for assessing sustainable human development beyond GDP. CCSI-02 integrates five dimensions: economic performance, human development, institutional quality, environmental sustainability, and social equity. The framework does not treat GDP as an inadequate statistic; rather, it repositions GDP as one component of a broader assessment of development. The paper formalizes the conceptual architecture of CCSI-02, specifies principles for indicator selection, directional normalization, dimension construction, aggregation, and weighting, and develops theoretical propositions that generate testable empirical implications. It further establishes a validation architecture covering construct validity, internal consistency, convergent validity, discriminant validity, external validity, predictive validity, and robustness. The paper explicitly separates measurement construction from subsequent econometric testing and does not claim empirical superiority over GDP or HDI without evidence. CCSI-02 is therefore presented as a testable theoretical and methodological contribution rather than as an empirically established replacement for existing development indicators. Future empirical research should evaluate whether CCSI-02 provides valid, robust, and policy-relevant information beyond established measures such as GDP and HDI.

title: A Framework for Evaluating Position Sizing Policies in Algorithmic Trading: A Monte Carlo Analysis of Compound Growth, Market Frictions, and the Opportunity Cost of Capital
affiliations: K. N. Toosi University of Technology

detail.title: A Framework for Evaluating Position Sizing Policies in Algorithmic Trading: A Monte Carlo Analysis of Compound Growth, Market Frictions, and the Opportunity Cost of Capital

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for the conduct of this study

detail.abstract: Comprehensive risk and performance evaluation of algorithmic trading strategies requires more than headline metrics such as cumulative return, the Sharpe ratio, or maximum drawdown; it demands rigorous treatment of position sizing, transaction costs, ruin probability, and drawdown dynamics under realistic trading conditions. A review of the literature reveals considerable heterogeneity in this regard: while some studies incorporate risk-controlled position sizing and transaction costs explicitly, others omit these elements entirely, producing backtests whose reported profitability can be substantially inflated. This study develops an open-source, Monte Carlo-based framework for evaluating money-management policies in algorithmic trading, moving from a frictionless theoretical expectancy criterion to a cost-adjusted, empirically simulated assessment of realized growth, drawdown, ruin probability, and capital utilization. Two competing position-sizing policies-fixed-dollar and percentage-of-equity-are compared, and a cost-adjusted Kelly criterion is derived to determine the optimal risk fraction. Applied to a representative reference strategy, the framework demonstrates that neglecting realistic transaction costs can overstate reported returns by a substantial margin, underscoring the risk of a false impression of profitability in cost-blind backtesting. All Python code underlying this framework has been released publicly in an open-source repository to support transparency and reproducibility in future research.

title: The Future of Cooling and Development Across the Global South: Why Affordable Thermal Comfort Is Becoming Essential Economic Infrastructure

detail.title: The Future of Cooling and Development Across the Global South: Why Affordable Thermal Comfort Is Becoming Essential Economic Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the research. The analysis was conducted independently under H Heuristics’ research program on climate adaptation and infrastructure economics.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study did not involve human or patient participants. All data used were secondary sources from public datasets (IEA, SEforALL, UNEP, IFC, WHO, and national policy documents). Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self‑funded by H Heuristics, with no external grants or institutional sponsorship.

detail.abstract:
Cooling is no longer a discretionary amenity; it has become load‑bearing economic infrastructure across the Global South. Rising temperatures, rapid urbanization, and expanding heat‑exposure have pushed thermal comfort into the same category as electricity, water, and transport—an essential precondition for food security, health‑system reliability, industrial competitiveness, digital‑economy growth, and labor productivity. As the report states, “adequate thermal comfort has become as structurally necessary to economic activity as electricity, transport, or water” .

More than 1.05 billion people are projected to fall into the highest cooling‑risk category by 2030, with another 2.83 billion experiencing limited or unreliable access. Household AC ownership in hot‑climate countries remains below 10%, compared to 91% in the U.S. and Japan, reflecting structural gaps in financing, grid reliability, and housing—not simply affordability. These deficits impose measurable costs: heat stress is expected to erase 2.2% of global working hours by 2030, equivalent to 80 million full‑time jobs and $2.4 trillion in lost output, overwhelmingly concentrated in South Asia and West Africa. As the report notes, “heat stress will cost the global economy the equivalent of 80 million full‑time jobs by 2030” .

Closing the cooling gap requires $400–800 billion in additional investment beyond current levels, yet efficient cooling could save $5.6 trillion in electricity costs and avoid $1.8 trillion in new generation capacity over 25 years. Technologies already exist—district cooling, passive design, decentralized solar cold storage, superefficient equipment—but deployment lags behind need. Policy frameworks such as National Cooling Action Plans, building codes, refrigerant standards, and tariff reform are emerging but unevenly adopted.

To operationalize cooling as infrastructure, the report introduces the CORE Framework:

  • Capitalize — mobilize infrastructure‑grade finance;

  • Optimize — raise efficiency and reduce refrigerant footprint;

  • Regulate — establish standards, codes, and national plans;

  • Expand — deliver last‑mile access through decentralized models.

Case studies from India, Rwanda, the UAE, Nigeria, and Kenya demonstrate how these pillars function at different scales. The report concludes by situating cooling within the Convergence Thesis: economies that close structural infrastructure gaps fastest converge fastest with high‑income peers. Cooling, once peripheral, is now a central determinant of economic resilience, productivity, and long‑run development trajectories.

title: Balancing Consumer Data Protection and Digital Trade: A Comparative Study of the WTO Agreement on E-Commerce and Regional Agreements

detail.abstract: This paper will attempt to analyze the compatibility between WTO's approach on digital trade, particularly Article 16, and regional frameworks including the GDPR in the European Union, the USMCA, and ASEAN's Digital Data Governance Framework. This study therefore highlights the fact that data protection for consumers complements the promotion of e-trade since data localisation and restrictions on cross border transfer of data begin to poison the root of liberalization of trade. Balance is one of the prime prerequisites of international trade policy and implies in consumer confidence and transparency in the world of electronic global economy.Despite the debates, what the literature shows is the need for a harmonious data protection system that combines well with digital tradethe existing frameworks show tensions, which could result in overreliance on certain practices. This study threefold: It evaluates the legal coherence of Article 16 of the WTO E-Commerce Agreement with regional data protection laws; it identifies the conflicts where data protection rules inhibit trade, specifically in the context of cross-border data transfer; and it suggests feasible harmonization mechanisms that uphold both trade openness and robust data privacy standards.This paper would engage the comparative legal analysis to determine key provisions of WTO E-Commerce Agreement, GDPR, USMCA and ASEAN frameworks.

title: Sustainable Development in an Age of Technological Abundance: Why Access and Diffusion Will Determine Who Benefits from Innovation

detail.title: Sustainable Development in an Age of Technological Abundance: Why Access and Diffusion Will Determine Who Benefits from Innovation

detail.abstract: Technological abundance is reshaping the foundations of sustainable development by expanding productive capacity, accelerating knowledge diffusion, and altering the relationship between human societies and ecological limits. This paper argues that emerging technologies—automation, AI, distributed manufacturing, and advanced energy systems—create new pathways for decoupling human well‑being from resource intensity, but also introduce systemic risks tied to inequality, governance failures, and rebound effects. Using a multidisciplinary framework that integrates development economics, systems theory, and ecological constraints, the study examines how abundance-driven growth can either reinforce or mitigate global polycrisis dynamics. The analysis highlights three structural levers: institutional adaptability, equitable access to technological capabilities, and the alignment of innovation with long‑term planetary boundaries. The paper concludes that technological abundance does not inherently guarantee sustainable outcomes; instead, sustainability depends on deliberate governance choices that channel surplus capacity toward resilience, social inclusion, and ecological regeneration.
