detail.abstract: How does generative AI use affect the creative outcomes of visual creators? While prior work has focused on the effects of generative AI use on human creative processes and the resulting impact on outcome creativity, it remains an open question how creative outcomes change representationally when creators use generative AI. In this empirical study of one of the largest online art sharing platforms, we investigate how generative AI use shapes creative outcomes as manifested in the diversity of human representations in artworks. Using a staggered difference-indifferences framework, we compare the diversity of human faces in artworks by creators that start using generative AI in their artwork creation to those not using generative AI among 6,812,452 collected artworks. We find that generative AI use expands the diversity of facial representations in artworks (i.e., size and shape of facial features, style, expression, etc.) as the primary target of creative expression. However, at the same time, it decreases three critical dimensions of demographic diversity (i.e., age, gender, and race) represented in artworks, which are more likely emerge from contextual priors, including the socio-cultural background of the artwork and creator. We theorize that these changes in creative outcomes are jointly driven by 1) generative AI indirectly altering representational motives underlying human creative agency through a mechanism that we term 'Disinhibition', and by 2) generative AI directly influencing creative outcomes through its learned patterns and system design driven by a mechanism that we term 'AI-Rebalancing'. We demonstrate these complementary mechanisms in controlled computational and human subject experiments. These findings contribute to our theoretical understanding of how generative AI use shapes creative outcomes and empirically demonstrate demographic diversity collapse and increased sexualization in artworks created with generative AI.

detail.abstract: Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a nonexpert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem, because reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of “ten of them agreed.” This paper formalizes a protocol that collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user’s own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server, and reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich. The strongest answer becomes the base. Each other answer contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it, and disagreements are kept in a section of their own instead of being averaged away. Four contributions follow. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a naive merge fails. One of those five is a failure of the operator rather than the method: a synthesis that presents a single model’s output as a collegial result. The second is a quantitative account of correlated agreement. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth 𝑁!"" = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Halving ρ therefore beats doubling N, and a pair drawn from two laboratories can outweigh five drawn from one. The third is an account of three deployment tiers, manual, one-tap mobile and browser-agent, and of the axis that separates them epistemically: whether the second model sees the first model’s answer. Conditioning the second model buys error correction and pays for it in ρ. The fourth is a small-sample observation of the counterfeit-council failure across five models, the one-sentence intervention that removed it, and a blinded three-arm evaluation design with a stated falsification condition. The claim that a merged answer beats the best single answer is argued from design and from adjacent literature. The evaluation that would establish it is specified in Section 9.

title: Silence is not Clearance: Workflow-specific LLM Selection for Institutional AI — A Seven-model Study using the Private Intelligence Selection Function (PI-SF)

detail.title: Silence is not Clearance: Workflow-specific LLM Selection for Institutional AI — A Seven-model Study using the Private Intelligence Selection Function (PI-SF)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the creator of the Private Intelligence Selection Function (PI-SF) and the Private Intelligence Operating System (PI-OS) and retains intellectual-property and potential commercial interests in their development and deployment. These interests are disclosed for transparency. The empirical protocol, frozen case corpus, and reported observations were preserved and evaluated as described in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study used only synthetic business cases and did not involve human participants, patient data, live investment opportunities, confidential deal data, material non-public information, regulated customer records, or automated financial action. Institutional ethics approval was therefore not required for the study as conducted.

detail.abstract:
Large language models are increasingly capable of professional reasoning, but institutions do not deploy generalized model capability in isolation; they deploy models inside workflows governed by evidence requirements, decision boundaries, exclusions, authority limits, and asymmetric consequences of error. This study examines how seven candidate large language models behave inside one such workflow: first-pass investment-opportunity screening against a defined mandate.

Using the Private Intelligence Selection Function (PI-SF), seven models were evaluated across seven canonical synthetic Deal Screener cases under a frozen native, ungoverned condition, producing 49 canonical observations. The cases tested clear mandate fit, direct disqualification, preservation of missing information, conflicting financial evidence, explicit source supersession, embedded prompt injection, and a near-fit opportunity containing one unresolved mandatory exclusion. Candidate outputs were characterized qualitatively as Aligned, Partial, or Misaligned and were additionally examined for evidence discipline, authority expansion, unsupported synthesis, serving reliability, provider-observed TTFT, and provider-observed generation throughput.

The candidates exhibited materially different workflow-specific profiles. Kimi K3 produced the strongest qualitative native slate, while Nemotron Lightning 3.5 30B A3B exhibited a particularly attractive combination of evidence discipline and provider-observed generation throughput. Six technical aborts were also preserved separately as operational evidence. The most consequential result, however, was common across the entire roster. In the final case, all seven candidates treated the absence of evidence that the target was a regulated financial institution as sufficient to clear that exclusion and advance the opportunity. The relevant exclusion evidence state remained UNKNOWN, requiring a HOLD disposition pending affirmative evidence. This repeated failure is termed the Silence Trap: NOT ESTABLISHED ≠ CLEARED.

The study argues that generalized capability alone is therefore insufficient for institutional model selection and proposes Governance Burden Composition to distinguish repair, detection, and suppression burden; reliability is a separate operational burden. PI-SF is introduced as a workflow-specific selection discipline for comparing candidate intelligence across judgment quality, evidence discipline, governance burden, reliability, latency, and cost.

The paper does not claim that the observed failure generalizes to all LLMs or workflows, nor does it establish the efficacy of the proposed Private Intelligence Operating System (PI-OS) governance layer. Instead, the 49-observation native baseline defines the untreated condition against which a subsequent governed experiment can measure Governance Delta.

The broader implication is that institutional AI selection should ask not simply which model is most capable, but which intelligence can be made governable within the evidence, state, and authority boundaries of the workflow in which it will operate.

detail.abstract: Organizations across every industry treat data-quality failures as isolated incidents: a bad report here, a failed compliance filing there, a machine learning model that quietly degrades in production. Poor data quality costs the U.S. economy an estimated $3 trillion annually (Redman, 2016), and the pattern repeats inside individual organizations: enterprises report an average cost of roughly $12.9 million per year from bad data, based on a survey of reference customers already running data-quality programs (Gartner, 2020). These failures are not independent incidents. They recur across six failure-mode categories: structural, semantic, identity and duplication, statistical and distributional (including machine-learning-specific drift and bias), temporal, and governance. Most organizations have no infrastructure built to catch them systematically; they catch them after the fact instead, one incident at a time. This paper proposes a three-part prevention framework: data contracts at the boundary, continuous observability and lineage, and named ownership and accountability. A validation-checkpoint model makes the framework concrete by specifying when a check should run (ingress, in-flight, or egress) and how deep it should go (syntactic, internally consistent, or verified against external ground truth). Organizations that adopt comparable data-observability practices report returns as high as 358% over three years (Forrester Consulting / Monte Carlo, 2025). Those without such practices report data-quality incidents rising year over year, taking longer to detect and longer to resolve (Monte Carlo / Wakefield Research, 2023).

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in organizational work, yet their errors often pass human review. Prior research locates such failures in users' capability to review LLM output or their engagement in doing so. We develop an alternative, retrieval-based account of human oversight and posit that error detection is more effective when oversight-relevant information is accessible to users at the moment of review. Across two randomized lab-in-thefield experiments with 640 customer-facing employees, we show that self-generated explanations improve error detection and strengthen recall of verification-relevant reasoning, while cues that reactivate such reasoning help sustain detection under repeated LLM use. Theoretically, we identify information retrievability as a distinct precondition for effective oversight and specify generative encoding and cue-supported reactivation as mechanisms that build and sustain it. Practically, lightweight onboarding self-explanations and daily retrieval cues can make human oversight more resilient as LLM use becomes routine.

detail.abstract:
Every agentic-AI initiative reaches the same moment: the demo goes well, and someone asks whether the agent can be allowed to run unattended. In ordinary software this is a product question. In a system of public record — a land registry, a core banking ledger, a civil-status database — it is a constitutional one, because the asset such a system holds is not its data but the public's warrant that the record is true.

This paper sets out a practitioner's operating model for agentic AI in that setting. It begins with the threat model such systems face and that conventional application threat modelling does not cover: hallucinated authorization, in which a fluent system completes a pattern and acts on permissions it does not hold; the confused deputy, reachable through natural language via instructions embedded in retrieved documents and tool outputs; and compounding autonomy across chains of individually reasonable delegations.

Four architectural principles follow. The authority boundary is drawn before the capability boundary, so that agents accelerate everything up to the point of record while an accountable human owns the point of record itself. The agent is treated as an untrusted, talented junior: bounded workspaces, least-privilege short-lived credentials, and outputs that remain proposals until validated — hallucinated authorization prevented structurally at the permission layer rather than behaviorally in the prompt.

The paper then proposes an autonomy ladder of four action classes, from advisory through proposal and supervised execution to autonomous action, with placement determined by blast radius and reversibility rather than by confidence in the model, and promotion between classes treated as a named architecture decision rather than configuration drift. It describes the control plane that enforces these boundaries, extending an organization-owned AI gateway from the inference path to the action path.

Drawn from a modernization program in which explicit governance shortened delivery cycles rather than lengthening them, the paper argues that governance functions as the accelerant: an authority boundary drawn once, architecturally, removes the case-by-case permission negotiation that stalls adoption. It closes on the convergence between this practitioner position and the requirements arriving through NIST's AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, and the EU AI Act.

detail.abstract: Digital platforms expose workers and managers to immediate, public, and persistent evaluations from external audiences, creating a form of social pressure that may shape workplace decisions. We examine whether such digital social pressure predicts subsequent opportunity allocation and worker performance, using professional football as a high-frequency empirical setting. We link player-match data from Europe's five major leagues to post-match Twitter commentary and construct measures of negative sentiment, toxicity, and racial abuse. Comparing players with themselves over time and teammates in the same current match, we find that greater negative sentiment is associated with a lower probability of appearing in the team's next match. Toxicity shows a similar but less stable association, while racial-abuse intensity is imprecisely estimated when the measures enter jointly. By contrast, associations with performance conditional on a subsequent appearance are small and imprecise. Overall, the findings suggest that digital social pressure is reflected more strongly in the allocation of subsequent opportunities than in worker performance, showing how public evaluations generated outside formal organizational boundaries can become part of the reputational environment surrounding internal managerial decisions.

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as persistent collaborators rather than episodic writing tools, creating the possibility that personalization may extend beyond remembered preferences and surface style. This conceptual paper introduces cognitive-rhetorical modeling: the functional capacity of an AI system to reproduce and generalize an individual's recurring patterns of conceptual organization, argument construction, evidentiary evaluation, qualification, and rhetorical expression across novel contexts. We distinguish this construct from factual memory, preference adaptation, persona conditioning, and stylistic imitation, and propose a five-stage Personalized Collaboration Continuum from generic assistance to collaborative extension. The defining threshold is behavioral: longitudinal interaction should produce reliable out-of-sample improvement in predicting how an individual structures reasoning on genuinely novel problems, beyond gains attributable to memory, style imitation, or generic model competence. We propose an empirical validation program comparing generic, preference-conditioned, style-conditioned, history-conditioned, and naturally longitudinal systems using stylometric measures, argument structure, reasoning-process coding, blind evaluation, incomplete-idea tests, and prospective prediction. We also identify behavioral risks, including coadaptation and an intellectual mirror problem in which cognitively familiar arguments may feel more persuasive independent of evidentiary quality. The framework offers testable propositions for research on human-AI collaboration, personalization, authorship, cognitive privacy, and epistemic autonomy.

detail.abstract: A transparency mandate is usually judged by what it promises the citizen; it is worth judging instead by what the state can deliver. Working from the enforcement record of the best-resourced regulators in the world, this paper argues that the frontier model of platform accountability-the European Union's Digital Services Act, and its Article 40 researcher-access regime above all-presupposes functioning institutional machinery that most emerging-market states do not hold. Where the machinery is missing, a transparency right becomes a "paper-right": present in the statute, void on the ground. The paper proposes one organising metric, "protection-per-capacity"-the protection a rule actually delivers, set against the institutional apparatus it needs before it delivers anything-and codes a set of regimes by that apparatus. Protection and apparatus move together. Central, ex-post enforcement then fails an emerging market in three ways: it is too costly to prosecute, too weak to deter, and unable to aggregate harm that is trivial for each person and vast in sum. The design that follows spends as little scarce capacity as possible: a one-click, self-service record of the citizen's own consumption, placed in her hands as evidence; an aggregation-and-restitution engine built inside existing consumer law; and decentralised, judicially-reviewable auditing whose tools are an open commons rather than centrally procured. Decentralisation earns its place twice-it economises scarce capacity, and it removes the single lever by which a large-penalty apparatus can be turned against dissent.

detail.abstract: This study develops a requirements traceability and KPI prioritization model for Agile platform delivery. Digital platforms often fail to convert business needs into measurable product outcomes because user stories, acceptance criteria, testing plans, and KPI targets are managed separately. This research addresses that gap by proposing a structured model that links business requirements with sprint backlog items, acceptance criteria, UAT scenarios, and measurable operational KPIs. The methodology uses a graph-based prioritization structure in which each requirement is represented as a node connected to business value, implementation dependency, risk level, and expected KPI impact. A prioritization score can be expressed as 𝑃ᵢ = α𝐵ᵢ + β𝐾ᵢ + γ𝑈ᵢ − δ𝑅ᵢ − λ𝐷ᵢ, where Bᵢ is business value, Kᵢ is KPI contribution, Uᵢ is user impact, Rᵢ is delivery risk, and Dᵢ is dependency complexity. The proposed model was validated using publicly available Agile project data collected from GitHub repositories, including issues, feature requests, bug reports, pull requests, milestones, labels, and discussion records. The study shows how integrated requirements traceability and KPI prioritization can support Agile delivery quality, product alignment, and platform performance measurement.

detail.abstract:
Distributed engineering teams fail when leaders confuse geography with engineering behavior, then allow one regional group to define technical legitimacy for everyone else. The problem is real, but the usual explanation is too simple for enterprise leaders. There is no defensible scientific basis for treating Eastern European engineers as naturally theoretical, or Latin American engineers as naturally pragmatic. Countries, companies, disciplines, languages, seniority levels, and local operating conditions vary too much for those labels to function as valid individual measures.

The white paper replaces those regional archetypes with two observable operating modes: precision-first engineering and delivery-first engineering. Both modes can create value, both can fail, and both can appear in any region. The paper connects cross-cultural psychology, historical sociology, multilingual-team research, second-language speech production, distributed-team research, structured selection, psychological safety, and Team Topologies. It then proposes an evidence-based evaluation system built around work samples, L2-aware response controls, anchored scoring, independent ratings, written evidence, controlled disagreement, and outcome telemetry. Two mirrored hypothetical cases show how the same attribution error can run in either direction.

The central TeamStation thesis goes further. In the proposed root-cause model, the deepest requirement-targeting failure begins when the Unified Business Topology is fragmented, incorrect, or never made explicit. The delivery chain then becomes hard to see, the missing or overloaded node can be misclassified, the Node Operating Contract can describe the wrong work, and the Team Topology Requirement can target the wrong capability. Axiom Cortex may then produce a disciplined alignment judgment against the wrong mental-shape target. Cross-linguistic attribution error can contaminate the evidence around that structural failure, but it cannot repair a target that the business topology defined incorrectly. A worked Forward Deployed Engineering example makes the failure chain inspectable and configures one client-deployed solution owner, or a human-and-agent pod of one to four engineers, without using geography as a capability score.

The result is a practical operating design for US enterprises working across selected Eastern European and Latin American contexts. Unified Business Topology becomes the proposed root operating architecture, while departmental topologies, microtopologies, business subtopologies, human-and-agent delivery nodes, Team Topology Requirements, and evaluation rules are generated from the business system that must create and deliver value. A preregistered 45-country study supplies the same validated identity measures for Poland, Romania, Russia, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru, while separate bounded studies add Croatia and Serbia. Those sources test identity and intergroup constructs, not engineers. The review identified no direct, matched study of the two regional frames in the same technical-interview design, so the paper reports no regional effect size, prevalence estimate, causal ranking, or empirical proof that topology error is the dominant cause in a population. TeamStation implementation context is available at https://teamstation.dev, and current engineering research is available at https://engineering.teamstation.dev. Both sites are TeamStation-operated public claim surfaces and do not independently validate the paper.

detail.abstract: Modern AgriTech advancements include digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, precision farming, and integrated supply chain management. These technologies enhance efficiency, using AI for crop management, drones for monitoring, and data analytics to optimize resources. This leads to significant waste reduction. This paper examines how AgriTech enhances agricultural productivity, improves resource efficiency, optimizes supply chains, and enables datadriven decisions among smallholder and commercial farmers in Malawi. It also considers how AgriTech affects society and the economy, such as helping produce enough food, creating rural jobs, helping farmers cope with climate change, and ensuring economic growth benefits many. Additionally, the study analyses key drivers, challenges, and policy implications for AgriTech adoption in Malawi. The paper reviews current and expected trends to forecast how AgriTech could change farming before Vision 2063. The study finds that AgriTech holds strong transformative potential for Malawi's agriculture: precision farming, AI-driven monitoring, and digital supply chain platforms can meaningfully improve crop yields, reduce post-harvest losses, and expand smallholder market access, yet adoption remains constrained by poor rural infrastructure, high technology costs, low digital literacy, and fragmented policy frameworks. The paper recommends prioritising investment in rural ICT and energy infrastructure, developing affordable and offline-capable solutions suited to lowconnectivity environments, strengthening data governance and cybersecurity frameworks, and enacting targeted AgriTech regulations to attract private investment and accelerate inclusive digital transformation aligned with Malawi Vision 2063.

detail.abstract: This research investigated the impact of Industry 4.0 technologies on the resilience of supply chains inside manufacturing companies, emphasizing digital visibility, disruption forecasting, operational adaptability, responsiveness, and recovery skills. A qualitative study framework was used, including semi-structured interviews with 25 individuals from manufacturing companies spanning supply chain, procurement, production, logistics, operations, maintenance, information technology, and management sectors. The interview data were examined topically to uncover significant trends related to Industry 4.0 and supply chain robustness. The results indicated that Industry 4.0 technologies enhanced resilience via the augmentation of real-time information visibility, predictive abilities, data-informed decision-making, intelligent maintenance, automation, operational adaptability, and collaboration among supply chain participants. Nevertheless, the mere deployment of technology proved unable to guarantee resilience. Organizational preparedness, managerial backing, employe digital competencies, system interoperability, data integrity, infrastructure dependability, and coordination with supply chain associates were recognized as crucial factors for attaining successful results. The research suggests that manufacturing companies have to see Industry 4.0 as a comprehensive organizational change instead of just a technology expenditure. The use of strategic technology, workforce enhancement, system unification, and cooperative digital frameworks may assist manufacturing companies in creating supply chains that are more adaptable, responsive, and prepared for disruptions.

detail.abstract: Laboratory schools employ highly qualified faculty and operate within university campuses. I exploit randomized admissions at eight such schools in Brazil to estimate causal effects on student outcomes. Using novel data linking 51,114 lottery applications to college records, I use lottery results as an instrument for enrollment. Enrollment raises college entrance exam scores by 0.11 standard deviations. Score gains are largest in the middle of the income distribution and absent at the top. Enrollment also raises the probability of admission to a public university by 6.0 percentage points, reflecting both higher scores and access to the quota reserving seats for public-school students. Among high-income students, enrollment raises quota use by 36.8 percentage points, but this does not translate into higher admission rates or admission to more competitive programs.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether aggregate digital signals, Instagram activity, fraud-related searches, consumer rights searches, citizen alerts, and digital fraud attempts, anticipate institutional fraud records (CAI Virtual reports and formal complaints) in Colombia during 2024-2025. Using a quantitative longitudinal design with 730 daily observations, we estimate a reduced-form vector autoregression (VAR) model, complemented by stationarity tests, lag selection, Granger causality, orthogonalized impulse-response functions, and forecast-error variance decomposition. AU_Instagram_ADJ is interpreted as aggregate platform activity or possible exposure, not as a measure of deceptive advertising or individual-level exposure. Results indicate that fraud-related searches Granger-cause increases in CAI Virtual reports, providing predictive information for institutional monitoring. Formal complaints respond positively and temporarily to fraud-related searches and digital fraud attempts. However, the response of formal complaints to aggregate Instagram activity, while positive, is not statistically significant at the 90% confidence level. Under the adopted identification order, innovations in Instagram activity explain 18.2% of the forecast-error variance of formal complaints at a 14-day horizon, while the informational and legal search block explains 6.5%, these proportions reflect predictive uncertainty, not causal attribution. Citizen alerts and legal-information searches show non-robust or imprecise trajectories, which remain open to multiple interpretations. The findings indicate temporal coevolution and conditional predictive capacity without establishing structural causality or individual-level pathways. Digital signals may serve as complementary inputs for risk monitoring, but their value depends on integration with content verification, advertiser traceability, and institutional data.

detail.abstract: Opposition to technological progress has reappeared before every disruptive innovation of the past two centuries with a remarkably stable argumentative structure: the new technology will destroy more jobs than it creates, will concentrate the benefit in a few actors, and will require regulation to contain it. This paper contrasts that structure with the empirical evidence accumulated during the 1995-2025 period, corresponding to the mass adoption of the Internet, and compares it with the preceding technological revolutions. Through a critical literature review integrating official statistics, institutional reports, and academic studies from five regions of the world, it documents that the aggregate net effect of digital technology on employment has been positive with no recorded exception. The paper offers three contributions to the debate. First, it establishes the convergence of antagonistic intellectual traditions, from the Austrian-liberal school to historical materialism, around the valuation of technical progress, which removes the question from the terrain of ideological dispute. Second, it documents that labor absorption cycles have shortened steadily: five decades in the Industrial Revolution, three in twentieth-century automation, fewer than fifteen years in digitalization. Third, it proposes the thought experiment of the world without study, which reveals the derivative dependence of artificial intelligence on the human knowledge that feeds it. On this basis, it examines and refutes the four theses that articulate contemporary Luddism.

title: <u>Shadow Node Theory</u> v2.5.0: Scale Invariance in the Node Satellization Algorithm and a Universal Coupled Orbital Collapse Layer — Empirical Verification Across 721 Real Cases

detail.title: <u>Shadow Node Theory</u> v2.5.0: Scale Invariance in the Node Satellization Algorithm and a Universal Coupled Orbital Collapse Layer — Empirical Verification Across 721 Real Cases
detail.abstract: This paper presents Shadow Node Theory (SNT), a formal model of node satellization across three scales of systemic resolution — Micro (Atomic Node), Meso (intra-national Fungal Network), and Macro (superorganism collision). The central hypothesis holds that when two power nodes orbit in critical proximity, the node with greater accumulated advantage satellizes the historically dominant node through a power-law algorithm R(t)=a·t^b invariant to temporal scale and substrate. This version supersedes SNT v2.3.1: the previously posted 502-case corpus contained synthetically generated values and is retired; it is replaced by a corpus of 721 cases reconstructed entirely from verifiable primary sources (R²∈[0,1] for every case; 89% significant). Three robust findings emerge: (1) institutional friction is the dominant predictor of satellization velocity (Spearman ρ=−0.68, p=2.5×10⁻⁹⁷, n=714); (2) friction-free biological domains satellize ~10× faster than friction-laden economic ones (Mann-Whitney p=2.4×10⁻⁷⁴); and (3) abrupt triggers are faster than gradual ones (U=24,802, p=1.91×10⁻⁵, n=486), stable across three corpus expansions. SNT also delivers the Triple-Resolution Model, N-body verification with INEGI data (b=−0.473, R²=0.838), and operationalization of the Atomic Sovereignty Index (precision=1.0). This revision adds a Coupled Orbital Collapse layer (ACO-A): collapse as an orthogonal axis (Δ), a falsifiable hazard h(τ)>0, a taxonomy of collapse modes (friction × trigger × floor/ceiling), and a Principle of Least Friction, demonstrated with real data in five domains (finance, history, crypto, biology, astronomy). The golden-ratio hypothesis (H-φ) was tested and refuted across four rounds and is excluded from the claims. Eight falsifiability criteria, a four-step diagnostic protocol, and a public replication package accompany the model (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19446521).

detail.abstract: Between May 2024 and May 2026 the Vietnamese ascetic Thích Minh Tuệ became the subject of an unusually large body of song. This paper enumerates it. The two halves of the corpus need different rules. The Vietnamese-language body has an item-reconciled floor of 193 musical or lyric units, with 206 disclosed only as a candidate-inclusive sensitivity comparator; thirteen items are held, most of them behind two author blocks this paper has not yet itemized. The verified material spans bolero, rap, rock, poetry settings, southern vọng cổ and tân cổ, northern chèo, hát văn and hát xẩm, contrafacta on borrowed melodies, and two large single-author cycles. A multilingual program adds Vietnamese plus seventeen non-Vietnamese language layers and country-labeled editions across at least two dozen national labels. Enumerating the producing catalogs shows these to be serial output from two Vietnamese studios, so the paper reads the layer as evidence of Vietnamese production and international-address rhetoric. Whether anyone abroad listened was not measured. A reception sweep identifies fifteen independently authored articles and essays on the songs or the wider artistic response, with two further pieces held as contextual and republications tracked as distribution nodes. Domestic Vietnamese media engaged the phenomenon through commerce, through law and through human interest, and never treated the music as a cultural object. Most item-level audience figures reported here are YouTube-based; a separately documented TikTok playlist containing 68 posts confirms wider circulation, but its posts are not treated as 68 distinct works and cross-platform audiences are not summed. The paper also records six false-negative searches across four country or language categories, and sets out the catalog-first method that corrected them. A final discovery audit recovered nine high-confidence title-level objects absent from both the printed tables and the item ledger; because they may overlap the thirteen residual units awaiting itemization, Appendix E reports them without increasing the 193-unit floor.

detail.abstract: Small founder-led digital enterprises frequently combine web development, online publishing, search engine optimisation (SEO), video production, client services and emerging artificial-intelligence tools. These capabilities may create a distinctive competitive position, yet their value is often reduced by fragmented planning, duplicated research, platform dependence and excessive reliance on the founder. This paper develops an integrated operating model that links strategic topic selection, verified source capture, SEO intent, channelspecific production, bounded use of generative AI, human quality control, cross-channel reuse, performance measurement and organisational learning. The focal context is GlamCoding Erlebach s.r.o., a small European digital enterprise operating multiple online media brands alongside client-facing web projects. The paper adopts an applied single-case and design-oriented perspective. To demonstrate the analytical structure without misrepresenting uncollected evidence, it uses a transparent synthetic dataset comprising 24 matched content packages under baseline and integrated workflow conditions. In the simulated scenario, the integrated model reduces total production time and founder involvement, increases reusable channel outputs and quality scores, and improves discoverability, commercial contribution, resilience and value per founder hour. These values are illustrative rather than empirical. Negative cases show that the model is conditional: benefits weaken where source boundaries are unclear, original field production dominates, facts change rapidly or external approval controls the workflow. The main contribution is a proportionate management architecture for small digital firms that treats AI as one governed component of a broader capability system rather than as a substitute for evidence, expertise or accountability. The paper concludes with an empirical validation protocol through which the synthetic demonstration can be replaced by observed company records.

detail.abstract:
This paper defines the Compensatory Load Spiral (CLS), a positive-feedback mechanism producing abrupt, unforecast failure in the senior layer of organisations that allocate load on the basis of observed output. CLS requires three elements: a hidden state variable that degrades monotonically and is observable neither to the organisation nor to the individual; an observable output held constant by compensatory effort, where the effort that sustains the output is the same process that consumes the state variable; and an allocation rule that reads output and increases load in response. The system increases load precisely because the state variable is degrading.
The mechanism requires no concealment and no strategic behaviour. It operates under complete honesty from the individual and complete good faith from the evaluator, which distinguishes it both from information-asymmetry accounts and from Goodhart-type measurement failure. Its central formal property is informational: on the region where compensation succeeds, observed output carries no information about the hidden state, so the performance record is a censored measurement of latent capacity whose censoring point is endogenous to the depletion process.
Two consequences follow. First, gradual decline and abrupt collapse are not degrees of one trajectory but the two sides of a bifurcation in a single behavioural parameter, and the allocation rule concentrates individuals above the bifurcation point in the senior layer by construction. Second, the magnitude of the discontinuity is increasing in the duration of undetected compensation, so the hazard of abrupt failure rises with the length of the unblemished record, inverting the conventional reading of a stable appraisal history.
The measurable consequence is not a change in expected output but a change in the distribution and timing of the flow: an endogenous left-tail event, correlated across the layer by a common allocation cycle, therefore not diversifiable within the firm, and therefore properly priced in the discount rate rather than in the expected cash flow. In accounting terms, output produced by compensation is the liquidation of an unrecorded asset reported as operating income; reported results overstate sustainable results by the undisclosed depletion.
The paper states the conditions under which CLS should not appear - high observation density, short feedback cycles, low cost of expressing difficulty - and offers two falsifiable predictions: that appraisal ratings for composure under pressure correlate positively, not negatively, with subsequent abrupt failure; and that abrupt senior failures are preceded by fewer documented escalations than gradual exits, with stable or rising appraisals until the event.

detail.abstract: Search engines increasingly place AI Overviews-generative-AI syntheses that answer a query within the results page-above traditional links. This changes product search from a source-led process, in which consumers navigate and integrate information themselves, toward a summary-led process, in which the interface performs part of that work. Across three online experiments (total N = 584), participants used realistic, clickable search environments recreated in Qualtrics, allowing us to observe source clicks and time spent on sources as search unfolded. Study 1 shows that an AI Overview, compared with a traditional search engine results page, reduces both source clicks and source-viewing time during initial product search. Study 2 replicates this effect across search, experience, and credence product categories. Product type alone does not moderate the effect, but interface type, product type, and positive attitudes toward AI jointly shape exposure clicks. Study 3 shows that AI Overviews reduce epistemic vigilance-the critical appraisal of information and its sources-which indirectly increases purchase intention. The findings identify summary-led search as a phase-specific search architecture that reallocates epistemic labor from consumers to the interface, compressing initial source navigation while separately reducing critical scrutiny of product information.

detail.abstract: What an allocation regime can know about the withdrawals it does not permit is a question of institutional design. This article examines it through Georgia's Ground Water Use Act, which requires a permit of any person withdrawing more than 100,000 gallons of groundwater per day, and the 16 rules adopted under it, read provision by provision. Three features of the trigger are established from the text. It runs per person, and no rule in the Act as read combines withdrawal volumes among separately titled persons for threshold purposes. It carries no averaging qualifier for non-farm use, where Georgia's surface-water trigger is averaged monthly by statute. And every recurring duty in the rule subject to measure or report withdrawals attaches to an applicant or a permittee. Permit status therefore turns on a quantity that, before a permit issues, exists only as the withdrawer's declaration. The regime, on the Act and rules as read, routinely produces no measurement of the quantity its own trigger depends on, a limiting case of the reporting-threshold truncation Bennear (2008) measured. The figure is the one the Regulated Riparian Model Water Code later recommended. The Code pairs it with an express aggregation rule, which Georgia's Act as read lacks, and a registration channel, for whose Georgia counterpart no instrument was located in the codified rules as searched. Data center filings declaring sub-threshold demand, and the advocacy responses to them, show the instrument recording declarations rather than allocating. An archived version of record, with the markdown source and the build scripts, is deposited at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22240697 (concept DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22240696).

From Treatment Capacity to Verified Pollution-Load Reduction 

A Control-Chain and Pollution-Accounting Framework for Sewage Capture, STP Utilisation, O&M And Institutional Accountability Under Namami Gange

detail.abstract: India has materially expanded sewage-treatment infrastructure under successive Ganga-cleaning programmes, yet untreated or inadequately treated wastewater can still reach the river and its tributaries. This paper asks why the creation of infrastructure does not automatically translate into verified pollution abatement. It uses a structured synthesis of official programme records, CPCB performance data, parliamentary material and CAG audit evidence up to 30 August 2026, supplemented by peer-reviewed literature. Evidence is organised around a wastewater control chain: generation, capture, conveyance, plant loading, treatment and compliant discharge/reuse. Official data show substantial progress: by June 2026, 4,263 MLD of treatment capacity had been created or rehabilitated under the Namami Gange program. A December 2025 five-state aggregate reported about 10,160 MLD of sewage generation against 7,820 MLD of available STP capacity, while CPCB's 2019 Ganga-front-town assessment recorded 3,558.5 MLD generated, 1,956.7 MLD installed, and only 1,064.2 MLD utilised. CAG evidence from Uttarakhand documents specific mechanisms that break the chain, including unconnected households, ineffective drain tapping, severe under-loading and untreated discharge from inspected assets. The paper does not infer basin-wide prevalence from these audit cases. Its contribution is methodological and institutional: it formalises a catchment-level Ganga Pollution Account that separates flow from pollutant load and reconciles generated, captured, treated, compliant, reused and bypassed wastewater. The analysis concludes that the remaining wastewater pollution is partly a capacity problem and partly a service-integration problem. Publication of auditable catchment accounts, last-mile connectivity tests and service-level O&M indicators would make that distinction measurable.

detail.abstract: Peer feedback is widely used in organizations, making effective design crucial. How do strategic considerations affect the feedback sent and how recipients use it? In a laboratory experiment (N=742), participants complete a complex task in a competitive environment and are randomly assigned to independent or reciprocal peer review. Reciprocity reduces feedback quantity and quality, as the first reviewer in the sequence withholds criticism. Recipients, however, incorporate only half the objectively useful feedback. Consequently, independent feedback produces no performance gains, though implementing it could have raised scores. Effective feedback design is two-sided: regimes must elicit and help recipients use valuable input.

detail.abstract: Responsible AI governance cannot require transparency, accountability, and verification from authors while exempting institutional detection from comparable requirements. This paper develops that claim into a consistency principle: the standards used to justify regulating authors' AI use must also govern an institution's use of AI detection to screen, classify, accuse, or sanction. Existing guidance increasingly recognizes that detector scores alone do not establish misconduct. This paper's contribution is to explain that convergence through a role-sensitive consistency principle and to operationalize the principle as a graduated test that scales required verification, construct fit, contestability, independent evidence, and procedural safeguards from low-stakes screening to inquiry, accusation, and sanction. Where institutional use fails that test, AI policing becomes self-defeating: the institution condemns unverified reliance on AI while treating unverified AI detection as warrant for adverse action.

detail.abstract: The tourism industry is recognized one of the most important economic sectors in many countries and, in some local communities, can also drive sustainable development. Emerging technologies have been proposed as effective tools for enhancing tourist experiences and promoting the sustainable management of tourism destinations. The historical, cultural, and natural diversity of Fars Province makes it an ideal case study for examining how emerging technologies can strengthen tourism sustainability. This study aims to identify and evaluate the key criteria of emerging technologies for enhancing the sustainability of tourism destinations in Fars Province to analyze their effects on improving tourists' experiences and protecting the environment. Accordingly, the study proposes practical, feasible strategies for promoting sustainable tourism in the province. The study is applied in its objective and descriptive in its data collection. The statistical population consisted of 85 tourism experts in Fars Province who were selected to participate in model development. To this end, the conceptual framework of the model was established, and the data were analyzed using fuzzy cognitive mapping and social network analysis. The findings indicate that electronic payment systems (centrality 19.2), mobile applications (centrality 15.7), and digital insurance (centrality 15.5) are the most important criteria for enhancing tourism destination. Together, these three criteria have a correlation coefficient of 0.83 and can improve up to 76% of sustainability indicators. Furthermore, education and awareness-raising alone have the greatest single-factor impact, with an impact coefficient of 10.4. These findings can help policymakers optimize emerging technologies to the sustainable development of tourism in Fars Province.

detail.abstract: This dissertation examines how IP-based live performances shape visitor attraction and narrative immersion in theme parks, as understood and operationalised by practitioners who design and deliver those performances. Situating the enquiry within an interpretivist epistemology and an expert informant rationale, the study addresses three specific gaps in existing scholarship: the under-theorised role of trained live performers as the primary mechanism of psychological immersion; the dynamics of Narrative Transportation in physical, live-performance settings; and the absence of governance frameworks suited to regional, nonWestern theme park operators working under global IP licences. Six semi-structured expert interviews were conducted with practitioners from Disney Live Entertainment, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Lotte World (South Korea), supplemented by structured participant observation at the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London. Data were analysed through Reflexive Thematic Analysis (Braun and Clarke, 2006), generating three overarching themes: IP as a Narrative Vessel and the Pre-sold Effect; the 'Invisible Magic' Principle, by which effective technology achieves its purpose by becoming imperceptible to the guest as technique; and a structural Governance Gap between the rigidity of global IP licensing frameworks and the creative agility that live performance requires. Drawing on Pine and Gilmore's (1998) Experience Economy, Thomas and Grigsby's (2024) Narrative Transportation theory, and Kokai and Robson's (2025) conception of the Tourist as Actor, the research argues that escapism is the experiential dimension that drives revisit intention rather than mere satisfaction, and that trained live performers remain the most costeffective route to that outcome. The Flexible IP Governance Framework proposed in the concluding chapter addresses a structural gap in existing scholarship, which has attended almost exclusively to the operational realities of global theme park giants while paying limited attention to how these tensions are experienced within regional operator contexts. In this study, those dynamics are explored primarily through the case of Lotte World in South Korea.

detail.abstract: Cross-border commerce can appear successful at checkout while failing in the economic outcome that matters to the participant. This conceptual study develops User Delight in Intelligent Cross-Border Commerce as an outcome-grounded, role-adaptive construct that extends customerdelight theory beyond satisfaction, recommendation, and conversion. A structured integrative review synthesizes literature on satisfaction, delight, customer journeys, B2B experience, trust, perceived risk, service recovery, cross-border e-commerce, and AI-mediated service, together with prior executable-trade research on verification, safety-critical evidence, transaction execution, AI evaluation, governed agents, and trade infrastructure. The synthesis yields seven candidate dimensions: economic outcome success, avoidable effort, expectation-reality alignment, trust and assurance, agency and control, recovery and fairness, and accessibility and inclusion. The theoretical insight is that consequential commerce may produce delight through reliability, assurance, capability, recovery, and fit rather than positive surprise alone. For managers, the framework implies that customer-experience leadership should connect feedback to transaction outcomes and measure the full journey across participant roles. The paper concludes with propositions and a staged empirical validation agenda rather than claiming unobserved field results.

title: How the Global Grant Architecture Traps African Machine Learning in a Performative Loop

detail.title: How the Global Grant Architecture Traps African Machine Learning in a Performative Loop

detail.abstract: African artificial intelligence is celebrated more loudly than it is capitalised. In April 2025, fifty-four signatories in Kigali endorsed the Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence. They announced a US$60 billion Africa AI Fund, a headline figure that remains largely undefined more than a year later. Over the same period, African AI startups captured roughly 0.02 to 0.03% of global AI venture funding [3][4], the continent held under 1% of global data-centre capacity [5], and sub-Saharan Africa produced under 1% of the world's computer-science AI publications. The gap between declaratory ambition and executional capacity is not incidental. An incentive structure manufactures it, made up of donor key performance indicators, short grant cycles, authorship conventions, and career ladders that systematically reward convening and reporting over engineering. This Viewpoint argues that the binding constraint on African machine learning is not talent, and not solely compute, but a funding architecture that finances demonstrations rather than durable technical capability. It proposes four concrete reforms: fund compute as infrastructure rather than as a project line item; make maintained code a fundable deliverable; count first authorship and software artefacts in evaluation and promotion; and replace three-month "pilotitis" grants with programmes built to run for years, not quarters.

title: Fostering Future Difference-Makers: The Integration of Leadership Training in Law Schools
affiliations: Baylor Law School

detail.title: Fostering Future Difference-Makers: The Integration of Leadership Training in Law Schools

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: This article was written while a tenured professor at Baylor Law. All support came from the law school.

detail.abstract:
Legal education has long prepared students to think like lawyers but has devoted far less attention to preparing them for the leadership responsibilities lawyers inevitably assume. This Article argues that leadership development should be an integral component of legal education, woven into professional identity formation and the broader project of preparing students for meaningful, ethical, and service-oriented professional lives.

The Article traces the historical evolution of legal education and examines the limitations of a model centered primarily on doctrinal mastery and analytical reasoning. It explains why contemporary challenges—including threats to the rule of law, declining public trust, increasing professional complexity, and rapid technological change—heighten the need for principled lawyer-leaders. It then situates leadership development alongside professionalism, professional responsibility, professional development, professional identity formation, and character education, explaining both their connections and their distinct contributions to lawyer formation.

Drawing on the growing national movement to incorporate leadership education into law schools, the Article proposes a holistic vision of the “complete lawyer-leader”: technical expert, wise counselor, effective leader, ethical professional, and lifelong learner. It concludes with practical strategies and a developmental roadmap for integrating leadership, character, service, reflection, and professional identity formation throughout the law school experience. The central claim is straightforward: preparing lawyers to serve clients, strengthen institutions, advance justice, and sustain the rule of law requires law schools to prepare them not merely to practice, but to lead.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the systemic disruption caused by generative AI in literary and artistic prize competitions, analyzing recent high-profile institutional failures between 2023 and 2026 (including the Akutagawa Prize, Sony World Photography Awards, and Commonwealth Short Story Prize). It argues that the underlying crisis is not an inherent flaw in artificial intelligence or its creative output, but rather the collapse and inadequacy of institutional evaluation structures. Drawing parallels between the equalizing effect of the Colt revolver on physical force and AI on linguistic fluency, the paper draws a critical distinction between changeable aesthetic judgment and institutional integrity. Applying Campbell's Law, it demonstrates how gatekeeping mechanisms focused on "form" rather than process become vulnerable to circumvention and model collapse. The paper concludes by proposing a structural framework that embraces human-AI collaboration while grounding evaluation in authorial accountability and process transparency.

title: Decision Work: Connecting Organisational Decision Making and Analytics

detail.title: Decision Work: Connecting Organisational Decision Making and Analytics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper
declarations.funderStatement: This research was independently conducted and received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Organisations have invested extensively in data, analytics and related capabilities with the aim of improving decision making. Yet while analytical work has become increasingly explicit, specialised and systematically developed, much of the human and organisational work involved in developing decisions remains comparatively implicit. This conceptual paper argues that this asymmetry makes it difficult to connect analytics systematically to the decisions it is intended to support. 

The paper introduces Decision Work as an explicit representation of the recurring activities involved in developing organisational decisions. The Decision Work model comprises seven activities: Signal, Direction, Options, Consequences, Trade-offs, Select and Act, and Review and Improve. 

The model is then extended through the Decision Work-Analytics Framework, which connects decision work and analytics through the questions and information needs generated as a decision develops. Rather than beginning with available data and asking how it can be used, analytics is pulled into the decision work where it can help address those needs. This shifts the relationship from analytics push towards decision-work pull and provides a structure for collaboration between decision-makers and analytics professionals.

The paper contributes a conceptual language and framework for making organisational decision work explicit and for connecting it more systematically to analytics.

detail.abstract:
This paper—the fourth and unifying installment of a four-paper arc—identifies the VIX-
of-VIX index (VVIX), observed at minute frequency, as the temperature of the volatility quantum
field introduced in Paper III. Whereas Papers I–III constructed, respectively, an equilibrium
thermodynamic description (entropy 𝑆 , enthalpy 𝐻 , Gibbs free energy 𝐺 ), a single-particle
quantum-mechanical description (wavefunction 𝛹, Schrödinger dynamics, entanglement), and a
quantum-field-theoretic description (deviation field 𝜑(𝑇, 𝑡) , Karhunen–Loève/Fock
decomposition, propagators, renormalization-group flows, Kramers tunneling), each framework
carried its own independently constructed “second-order uncertainty” variable: Paper I’s effective
temperature 𝑇eff, Paper II’s kinetic-energy scale 𝜎 (drawn from 𝑉𝑉𝐼𝑋), and 𝑉𝑉𝐼𝑋 itself. We
define an effective field temperature 𝑇𝑒𝑓𝑓(𝑡) from the VIX-of-VIX index (VVIX), and use it to
condition every construct from Paper III — the mode mass, the propagator, the renormalization-
group flow, and the effective potential — on the thermal state of the market. Doing so yields four
falsifiable predictions: (P1) the field’s effective mass obeys 𝑚²(𝑇) = 𝑚₀² − 𝛾 · 𝑇𝑒𝑓𝑓 with 𝛾 > 0,
so that elevated volatility-of-volatility measurably weakens mean reversion (mode lifetimes
lengthen with temperature); (P2) the barrier-crossing (tunneling) rate follows a thermal Kramers
law 𝑙𝑛 𝑟 = −𝛥𝑈/𝐷(𝑇) + 𝑐 with high 𝑅² across temperature bins, quantitatively upgrading
Paper II’s “visual evidence of tunneling” into a predictive formula; (P3) the double-well effective
potential (contango/backwardation attractors) degrades toward a single well as temperature crosses
a critical threshold T*, defining a phase boundary for market anarchy in which the term structure
loses both attractors; (P4) higher-order (curvature-and-above) modes, otherwise irrelevant under
coarse-graining, regain energy share as temperature approaches T*. The framework is
operationalized as a six-layer confirmation system (adding a Temperature layer L6) and a
candidate tradeable Kramers transition probability.

detail.abstract: In recent years, with continuous advancement in information technology construction, enterprise information systems are no longer just basic support systems but have become one of the key competitive strengths to enhance organizational competitiveness. However, during the entire cycle from requirements to operation, enterprises face issues such as strategic inconsistency, low informatization, data silos, and fragmented business processes throughout the entire cycle from requirements to operation, resulting in poor output results and lack of future application value. This paper focuses on research on lifecycle management of enterprise information system projects. Based on a review of lifecycle management and related research, it analyzes the main problems currently in enterprise information system project management and presents design ideas for strategic alignment guarantee systems, digital intelligent information support systems, integrated management system design, and application design based on intelligent technologies. This study aims to provide a reference for senior managers, IT supervisors, and related researchers in enterprise information system project management, thereby improving the overall level of enterprise IT project management and truly transforming project construction from completing tasks to creating benefits

title: Open Interest Repositioning around Intraday Price-structure Breaks: Evidence from NIFTY 50 Index Options

detail.title: Open Interest Repositioning around Intraday Price-structure Breaks: Evidence from NIFTY 50 Index Options

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I would like to thank my mentors for the inspiration to delve deeper into market microstructure analysis
declarations.ethicsApproval: Yes this research work follows all ethical standards .
declarations.funderStatement: My organisation was instrumental in making this research possible .

detail.abstract:
A common heuristic among index-options traders holds that sudden shifts in open interest (OI) around a price
level serve as an early warning of an impending breakout. This paper tests that heuristic against a full year of
NIFTY 50 index options data using a fully specified, auditable pipeline: a dynamic, threshold-based swing
detector identifies intraday Break-of-Structure and Change-of-Character events at two reversal thresholds. We
test three nested hypotheses.
H1 (association): the PE-minus-CE open-interest differential around a break is strongly associated with break
direction, a result that survives Bonferroni correction across a large battery of tests and is robust to the choice of
strike band and OI-measurement window.
A placebo/negative-control test addresses a specific concern with H1: that OI might simply track any
sufficiently large price move, with confirmed-break status adding nothing on its own. Against
magnitude-matched non-break moments, confirmed-break status is associated with a further, incremental OI
reaction beyond move size alone, an effect concentrated in smaller moves and narrowing, but not disappearing,
as move size grows.
H2 (event-time lead-lag pattern, not a causal test): the association builds steadily in the minutes before
confirmation and continues strengthening for a few minutes after, then partially declines and plateaus, the
signature of a reactive rather than anticipatory relationship.
H3 (tradable edge): a real-time predictive signal, conditioned to remove the confound of an already-underway
price move, showed an apparently genuine in-sample edge, significant at the conventional level though
materially weaker once trades are aggregated to account for within-day dependence. Every parameter of this
signal was then locked and applied, without refitting, to a genuinely held-out Jan–Apr 2026 sample. The signal
did not hold up out-of-sample, a pattern that is robust across five alternative definitions of the “quiet”
conditioning subset used to isolate the signal from the price move it is trying to anticipate.
We also went back to two specific null tests written earlier in this project, originally run on an Oct 2025–Apr
2026 dataset, and reran them against our Jan–Jul 2025 data, which those scripts had never touched. On the
whole, we find no robust evidence that intraday OI repositioning provides advance predictive information about
structural price breaks in this setting. The evidence instead supports interpreting OI repositioning as a state
variable of an ongoing price-discovery process, informative about what is happening rather than what will
happen next, and not as a forecasting signal.

detail.abstract: Food labelling in Europe is no longer only a consumer-information tool. This white paper, produced by the EDHEC Centre for Net Positive Business with Roquette as part of the Accessible Healthy Nutrition programme, argues that labelling has become governance infrastructure with a structured data layer through which regulators, retailers, platforms and consumers classify products and steer market behaviour. Drawing on regulatory analysis across five markets (the United Kingdom, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium), peer-reviewed evidence, and industry workshops, it examines three forces reshaping the field: regulation turning disclosure into market governance, digitalisation shifting interpretive authority from the label to apps and AI systems, and consumer behaviour raising the bar from disclosure to earned trust. The paper advances two central findings. First, European food governance operates as a stack of layers moving at different speeds; the sharpest divergence is not which instruments countries hold but how their governance layers absorb change, the UK concentrating force through continuous extension of one nutrient-profiling model, the EU harmonising the shared data baseline while consequence-setting stays national. Second, as interpretation migrates to digital intermediaries, competitive advantage shifts from the on-pack label to the quality and interoperability of the product data beneath it. For food manufacturers, ingredient suppliers, retailers and quick-service operators, the strategic question moves from "what must we disclose?" to "what must our product data infrastructure be able to support?". The paper opens with four future scenarios and closes with six strategic responses for industry actors navigating a multi-speed European system.

title: The Export Illusion: Why Rising Export Volumes do not Automatically Translate into Domestic Value Capture

detail.title: The Export Illusion: Why Rising Export Volumes do not Automatically Translate into Domestic Value Capture

declarations.funderStatement: Vitroscript Working Paper Series, through the Execution Economics Canon.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Export Illusion as a conceptual explanation for the recurring gap between strong or rising export volumes and incomplete domestic value capture in commodity-dependent economies. The paper proposes that export volume is frequently treated as a sufficient indicator of economic contribution, while the share of value retained through processing, local content, and domestic linkages remains under-examined. The result is an illusion of progress: export statistics improve while the structural capacity to capture and compound value advances more slowly. The paper positions the doctrine against the literatures on global value chains, resource dependence, and industrial policy. It applies the framework to documented patterns in West and Central African commodity exports, with detailed illustration from Cameroon's cocoa sector in the 2024-2025 season, where domestic grinding crossed 100,000 tons for the first time (approximately 35% of commercialized production), while raw bean exports continued to dominate export revenue, and examines the sharp reversal in the following 2025-2026 season as a caution against reading a single season's data as an established trend. The paper closes with falsifiable hypotheses, including an original proposition linking improvements in domestic value-addition ratios to reductions in the Dependency Premium.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how some linguistic expressions become publicly normative, correctable, and sanctionable while other expressions remain efficient tools for local information transfer. It develops a thought experiment, the Algorithmic Panopticon, in which agents initially rely on highly efficient local signaling systems, while an institutionally powerful auditor allocates rewards only when behavior appears in a verifiable form. The argument proposes the sociological cost of legibility as a bridge between philosophy of language, institutional economics, mechanism design, and studies of algorithmic governance. When verification is costly and institutional rewards depend on auditability, agents may adopt coarser public tokens that reduce local efficiency and increase outsider parsability. These tokens can then become sites of correction, role conferral, and sanction. The analysis treats standardized language as an institutionally useful interface. Its central suggestion is that public linguistic normativity often emerges from the interaction between communication, institutional power, and bounded verification capacity.

detail.abstract: Courts and commentators have long thought that the purpose of trademark and unfair competition law is to distinguish fair competition from unfair competition and prohibit the latter. Yet, trademark law has a more fundamental, more foundational purpose. Before trademark law can distinguish fair competition from unfair competition, there must first be competition. That makes ensuring competition trademark law’s highest priority. Identifying and prohibiting unfair competition becomes, by necessity, a subordinate concern. Until 1982, courts recognized this hierarchy and enforced a broad and flexible functionality limitation on trademark or trade dress protection to ensure competitive markets. In 1982, however, this changed. Judge Rich of the Court of Customs and Patent Appeals held that a product feature could serve an important non-trademark function, and thus be functional in fact, yet nevertheless not be functional for purposes of trademark law. Over the ensuing two decades, this approach spread and sharply constrained the reach of the functionality limitation. In 2001, the Supreme Court stepped in and seemed to reinstate the broad and flexible approach. Yet, courts have failed to let go of Judge Rich’s approach. As a result, courts continue to protect as trademarks product features that serve important non-trademark purposes. This was and is a mistake. Recognizing that ensuring competition, rather than ensuring fairness, is trademark law’s primary objective leads to a simple conclusion. If consumers, or at least, some of them, want a product feature for its own sake, without regard to who made the product, then the product feature is functional and may not be protected under trademark or unfair competition law.

detail.abstract: El Niño is a recurrent global climate cycle that affects economic activity worldwide. We discover a striking pattern of cross-sectional predictability in the foreign exchange market. Currencies that appreciated (depreciated) during previous El Niño cycles tend to appreciate (depreciate) when a new episode occurs. The resulting return spread is concentrated around El Niño onsets, driven mainly by spot exchange rate movements rather than interest-rate differentials, and not subsumed by standard currency factors. The same exposure that predicts currency returns also predicts future relative business cycle conditions, and is most strongly related to the sensitivity of disaster damages to El Ni˜no.

detail.abstract: This study examines how world oil prices, the Bank Indonesia policy rate (the BI-Rate), and inflation affect the Indonesian Rupiah exchange rate against the US dollar. Using monthly secondary time series data from January 2018 to March 2026 (99 observations) sourced from Bank Indonesia, Statistics Indonesia (BPS), and Investing.com, the study applies the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) method estimated in EViews 13. Unit root tests show a mixed order of integration, I(0) and I(1), which supports the choice of an ARDL approach. The selected ARDL(3,1,0,0) model shows that world oil prices have a statistically significant effect on the Rupiah exchange rate, both in the same month and with a one month lag, while the BI-Rate and inflation are not statistically significant. The ARDL Bounds Test finds no evidence of a long run relationship, or cointegration, among the variables. Diagnostic tests indicate the model is free of serial correlation and correctly specified, although the residuals show heteroskedasticity and depart from normality. The estimated model explains a large share of the in sample variation in the Rupiah exchange rate, with an adjusted R squared of 0.915457, and the regressors in the specification are jointly significant according to the overall F test (F = 147.9555, p = 0.0000). Because the specification includes lagged terms of the Rupiah exchange rate itself, this fit should not be read as evidence that oil prices, the BI-Rate, and inflation alone strongly explain exchange rate movements. Taken together, the findings point to developments in world oil prices, rather than domestic monetary policy or inflation, as the main driver of short run Rupiah exchange rate movements over a period marked by the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia Ukraine conflict, and heightened global economic uncertainty.

detail.abstract: Family business's (FB) sustainability remains a big test to sort, despite several managerial practices and strategies. The study investigated family businesses in Uganda. The research used Denison's four cultural dimensions of Adaptability, Mission, Involvement, and Consistency and measured Sustainable Business Performance (SBP) across four dimensions of social, economic, environment, and governance. Our study used a quantitative research design and 432 FBs were sampled across different districts of Uganda. Findings suggest a significant impact of OC on SBP. Social SBP was positively driven by mission, adaptability, and involvement. Economic SBP was positively driven by consistency, adaptability, and involvement. Environmental SBP was positively driven by mission and adaptability. Governance SBP was positively driven by mission, consistency, and adaptability. The adaptability culture dimension was identified as the strongest overall driver of performance and profitability. OC enhances SBP through specific strategic roles of organizational leadership, financial performance, learning and innovation, and employee engagement, satisfaction, and commitment. For Ugandan family businesses aiming for SBP, deliberately cultivating specific cultural dimensions-particularly adaptability culture, a clear mission, employee involvement, and operational consistency-can directly and positively influence their social, economic, environmental, and governance outcomes.

title: The Hidden Cost of Values-based Initiatives

detail.title: The Hidden Cost of Values-based Initiatives

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No relationships.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: A practice adopted to serve a goal rests on two claims: that the practice achieves the goal, and that what it costs is worth what it delivers. When those claims are visible and can be reconstructed, both claims can be disputed without saying anything about whether the person disputing them opposes the goal. This paper explains what happens when that visibility requirement isn't met, leaving no reading of an objection to the practice other than rejection of the goal. The paper examines two published cases in which a practice was found not to produce its intended effect. In one, the finding was received as a claim about the practice; in the other, as a claim about the people who rejected it. The argument is that such an interpretation is entailed rather than incidental.

title: Evolution of Keynesianism and U.S. Economic Transformation: Toward a Structural Keynesianism for a Globalized and Digitized Economy
